nodes.start_phrase: The two figures (end of year 2024) below show Belfius Insurance’ total insurance coverage and assets exposed to climate risks.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose: Present a climate stress test designed to assess the impact of a severe climate-related scenario on Belfius Insurance’s solvency.
- Scenario design: Custom-built, inspired by NGFS and national supervisory scenarios; combines elements of a “disorderly transition” with immediate policy implementation.
- Scenario storyline:
  - Starts with an unprecedented Northern Europe storm causing deadly floods.
  - Triggers abrupt, stringent EU transition regulations targeting high GHG emitters due to public pressure.
  - Profitability of GHG-intensive firms declines; knock-on effects via higher energy/resource costs hit broader corporates.
  - Financial market impacts: equity market downturns and widening corporate credit spreads.
  - No supportive technological breakthroughs; persistent structural economic weakness.
  - Deterioration in European sovereign fiscal positions and debt quality.
  - Progressive increases in reinsurance program costs.
- Calibration approach: Financial and real asset shocks sourced from national supervisors and internal stress tests, given NGFS lacks specific shock calibrations.
- Risk identification and assessment results (general):
  - 2024 assessment references end-2023 positions; exposures shown via figures for total insurance coverage and assets subject to climate risks.
  - Expectation that 2025 results (based on end-2024 data) will be broadly unchanged.
  - Summary table evaluates transition and physical risks over short term (0–3 years) and long term (beyond 10 years) by activity domain, highlighting high/very high material risks.
  - Definitions of exposure scopes: Life equals all amounts insured against death; Non-Life equals all amounts insured in property and motor.

nodes.title: Climate Risk Assessment – General Results
nodes.heading: a. Climate Risk Assessment – General Results
nodes.start_phrase: The two figures (end of year 2024) below show Belfius Insurance’ total insurance coverage and assets exposed to climate risks.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Belfius Insurance’s climate risk assessment, stress testing, and disclosure within Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report Sustainability Statement.
- Climate stress test scenario: A catastrophic Northern Europe storm/flood triggers immediate, stringent EU transition regulations penalizing GHG emitters. Consequences include equity market declines, wider corporate credit spreads, lack of supportive technological breakthroughs, persistent economic weakness, deterioration of European public finances, and progressively rising reinsurance costs. Scenario aligns with NGFS “disorderly transition” but with immediate policy application; shocks sourced from national supervisors and internal calibrations.
- Risk identification and assessment: 2024 assessment based on end-2023 exposures; 2025 results expected to be broadly unchanged. Coverage and asset exposures to climate risks mapped across activity domains for short term (0–3 years) and long term (>10 years).
- Physical risk:
  - Overall short term at most medium due to Belgium/Europe exposure; key hazards: windstorms, river/pluvial/coastal floods, hail; other hazards (tornado, subsidence, wildfire) have lower impact.
  - Non-Life Insurance: Very high exposure (mandatory catastrophe cover in home insurance). Risk mitigated by strong reinsurance, annual contract adjustments, and a Belgian legal liability cap (~EUR 167 million) for flood events. Stress tests show Solvency Ratio and P&L volatility within risk appetite; long-term risk could rise with higher event frequency/severity and costlier/weaker reinsurance. ST: Medium; LT: High.
  - Life Insurance: ST: Low; LT: Medium even with hazard score increase.
  - Assets: Physical risk ST: Low; LT: Medium given limited overall impact and vulnerability.
- Transition risk:
  - Low for insurance activities; mainly concentrated in assets (equities, corporate bonds, direct property).
  - Overall short-term resilience is sufficient, but close monitoring is needed as physical risks may rise and transition dynamics add valuation/yield uncertainty to significant investment segments.
- Climate stress test result: Under the severe scenario, Solvency II ratio drops materially at end-2023 but remains within risk appetite due to reinsurance protections and market risk management.
- Disclosure approach (excluding unit-linked):
  - Equities/Corporate bonds: exposure measured by share invested in Climate Policy Relevant Sectors (CPRS) via NACE codes (not all CPRS firms face high risk).
  - Mortgages: high transition risk defined by EPC/proxy >400 kWh/m² with indexed LTV >80%, or unknown EPC (pre-2017) with indexed LTV >80%.
- Asset-class transition risk assessments:
  - Equities/Corporate Bonds: High transition risk; top 20 positions reviewed for sectoral exposure, transition strategies, regulatory sensitivity, carbon pricing, raw materials, and technology. Portfolio vulnerability lower than an index-based portfolio but still high.
  - Direct Property: Active energy-efficiency upgrades reduce vulnerability; risk assessed Medium (vulnerability score reduced to high).
  - Government Bonds: High transition risk, mitigated by strong credit quality and relatively low physical risks in holdings; severe but plausible stress tests remain within risk appetite.
  - Mortgages: Medium transition risk; stress testing shows no material solvency impact.
- Overall conclusion: Short-term resilience is adequate; long-term vigilance is required as physical hazards likely intensify and transition uncertainty could materially affect asset valuations and returns.

nodes.title: Climate Stress Test Result
nodes.heading: b. Climate Stress Test Result
nodes.start_phrase: The impact of the Climate Stress Scenario on the Solvency II (SII) ratio of Belfius Insurance is quantified.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Belfius Bank Annual Report 2024, Sustainability Statement, focusing on Belfius Insurance’s climate risk assessment.
- Overall resilience: Short-term resilience to climate risks is sufficient, but ongoing monitoring is required as physical risks are expected to rise and the low‑carbon transition adds valuation/yield uncertainty.
- Climate Stress Test: A severe climate scenario leads to a significant drop in the Solvency II ratio at end-2023, yet it remains within risk appetite due to the reinsurance treaty and market risk management.
- Disclosure approach: Explains and discloses percentages of non–unit-linked assets exposed to transition and physical risks.
  - Equities and corporate bonds: Exposure identified via Climate Policy Relevant Sectors (CPRS) using NACE codes; top 20 positions reviewed for transition strategy, regulation sensitivity, carbon pricing, input costs, and technology shifts. Portfolio vulnerability is lower than an index-based portfolio but risk remains high.
  - Mortgages: High transition risk defined as EPC >400 kWh/m² with indexed LTV >80%, or missing EPC (pre‑2017) with indexed LTV >80%. Stress tests show no material solvency impact; risk assessed as medium.
  - Direct property: Asset-by-asset vulnerability review (contract duration, energy efficiency, tenant quality); active energy-efficiency improvements lowered vulnerability; overall risk considered medium.
  - Government bonds: Good credit quality and lower physical risks in invested countries mitigate impacts; transition risk assessed as high but within risk appetite under severe yet plausible stress tests.
- Conclusion: High transition risk for equities/corporates and government bonds; medium risk for mortgages and direct property; solvency remains resilient under tested scenarios.

- Qualitative risk assessment:
  - Equities & corporate bonds: high transition risk; top 20 positions reviewed; portfolio vulnerability lower than an index-based portfolio but still high.
  - Direct property: risk reduced to medium after energy efficiency improvements; vulnerability score decreased.
  - Government bonds: transition risk high but within appetite; mitigated by strong credit quality and relatively low physical risks in relevant countries.

nodes.title: Mitigation Action
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.4. Mitigation Action
nodes.start_phrase: Incorporating ESG and climate considerations into business and risk practices is key to mitigate risk at the source.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on climate risk exposure across Belfius Insurance’s asset classes and how these risks are assessed:
  - Transition risk: defined for direct property via energy efficiency and lease characteristics; for listed assets via ESG/climate criteria. Metrics reported: Equity & corporate bonds 36.8%; Direct property 12.5%; Mortgage loans 2.4%.
  - Physical risk: defined via Belgian regional flood maps for direct property and mortgage loans. Metrics reported: Direct property 0.0%; Mortgage loans 2.6%. All direct property assets are in Belgium.

- Mitigation actions integrating ESG and climate across investments, insurance, and lending:
  - Investments: embed ESG/climate criteria in equities, corporate bonds, government bonds, and funds; support issuers’ transition and Paris alignment; conduct due diligence for direct property; invest in certified sustainable buildings (LEED/BREEAM); implement resilience planning; 2024 plan approved to improve direct property energy efficiency.
  - Non-life insurance: incorporate climate in pricing/underwriting (home, motor); mitigate physical risks via robust reinsurance and annually renewable contracts; ongoing monitoring of evolving physical risks.
  - Mortgage lending: consider location-based climate exposures, set energy efficiency requirements, and incentivize borrower mitigation.
  - Governance and frameworks: align with Group ESG Framework, ESG Risk Management Framework, Transition Accelerations Policy, and Risk Appetite Framework; leverage Belfius Insurance ESG team, Group ESG Central Team, and ESG Risk Competence Centre.
  - Status: ESG risks currently within risk appetite; commitment to enhance methodologies and reporting, with emphasis on climate.

- Non-financial resilience analysis overview:
  - Purpose and structure: assess Belfius Group’s operating model resilience to climate change; describe scope/methods (including scenario use), results by non-financial risk, key figures on assets at material physical risk, and mitigation/action plans.

- Scope and methodology details:
  - Climate and Environmental Risks Materiality Assessment (CERMA): expert-based, top-down assessment of non-financial risks across own assets, operations, and third parties; focuses on IT, buildings, suppliers, delivery processes, and liability. Two-step approach:
    1) Identify transmission channels affecting people, buildings & facilities, and processes (IT/outsourcing).
    2) Assess impacts on risk clusters in the Belfius Risk Taxonomy: IT & infrastructure, execution/process management, fraud, employment practices & safety, client products & business practices, public safety, and reputation.
  - Operational risk climate assessment: bi-annual threat analysis of physical risks (e.g., floods, natural disasters) on data centers and buildings to support business continuity, using expert judgment and data like flood maps and proximity to risk features.

- Supplier and third-party resilience:
  - Procurement integrates ESG criteria; updated Sustainability Code of Conduct (2023); vendor ESG assessments via EcoVadis and scorecard monitoring.
  - New Third Party Risk Management framework assesses suppliers’ resilience, including existence, testing, and auditing of Business Continuity Plans, scenario coverage, business impact analyses, subcontractor dependencies, and overall resilience maturity.

nodes.title: Disclosure of assessment
nodes.heading: 2.3.2.3. Disclosure of assessment
nodes.start_phrase: The following table shows the result of the flood risk assessment realized on all significant assets of Belfius in Belgium.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Results of Belfius Bank’s climate and environmental (C&E) risk identification and assessment, related disclosures, mitigation actions, and integration of ESG into business activities.

- Physical risk assessment:
  - Potential disruptions to Belfius’ operations and those of suppliers/third parties, with emphasis on critical third-party infrastructure and subcontractors in areas prone to extreme events.
  - Indirect HR impacts (sickness, transport and housing disruptions from floods/heatwaves), affecting absenteeism, well-being, and productivity.
  - Physical C&E risks expected to be materially impactful mainly in the long term.
  - Bi-yearly analyses indicate flood, wildfire, and earthquake risks for Luxembourg data centers are adequately mitigated.

- Transition risk assessment:
  - Transition risk drivers (e.g., customer preference shifts) assessed as most impactful on non-financial risk (NFR) clusters—especially IT & infrastructure and execution/process management.
  - Execution risks in implementing ESG strategy and products; supply chain issues (component/raw material shortages, delivery delays); risks expected to peak in the medium term.
  - Longer-term risks from product/service substitution with lower-emission options leading to IT, energy, and supply chain disruptions.
  - Heightened reputational and potential legal risks if ESG expectations are unmet, with possible effects on investor interest and talent retention.

- Overall NFR assessment:
  - C&E impacts on NFR clusters rated moderate; mitigation actions in place and monitored.
  - NFRs generally have higher velocity (exposure and mitigation) than credit risks, reducing risk except for certain assets (e.g., HQ and critical ICT providers).

- Disclosure: Flood risk for Belgian assets:
  - Assessment of 485 significant buildings (HQ and agencies; excluding independent DVV agencies), using methodology aligned with financed assets; insurance mitigants not considered.
  - Results: 55 locations at high risk, 44 at medium risk; 20.41% of locations at high/medium flood risk.

- Mitigation actions:
  - Robust business continuity and crisis management aligned with ISO 22301 and BCI Good Practice Guidelines; dual-office and remote working strategies; detailed plans, exercises, and reporting.
  - Threat-prioritized action plan including tech upgrades, policy updates, staff training, allocated resources, monitoring/evaluation, stakeholder communication, incident response, and thorough documentation.
  - Strengthened supplier management via ESG due diligence: updated Procurement Policy (since 2020), Supplier Sustainability Code of Conduct, EcoVadis assessments/scorecards, and KRI tracking.
  - ESG Risk Management Framework established in 2023 (defining three lines of defense), updated in 2024 to include Belfius Insurance.

- Integration of ESG into business activities:
  - Transition Acceleration Policy (TAP) applied group-wide to financing, investing, and insurance with professional counterparties, steering towards low-carbon activities and limiting harmful ones.
  - Criteria embedded in lending, investment, and insurance decisions; sector/sensitive activity screening based on UN Global Compact’s 10 principles.
  - Commitments to UNEP FI PRB, PSI, and PRI.
  - Cross-functional development involving ESG, procurement, legal, and communications to embed responsible business practices.

nodes.title: Mitigation Action
nodes.heading: 2.3.2.4. Mitigation Action
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius is committed to ensuring the continuity and resilience of its critical business activities, in full compliance with Belgian regulations.
nodes.summary:
- Reports exposure of Belfius Bank’s locations to flood risk: 55 locations at high risk, 44 at medium risk, with 20.41% of total locations in high or medium risk categories.
- Details a comprehensive mitigation and business continuity approach aligned with ISO22301 and BCI Good Practice Guidelines, applied across all entities, featuring dual-office and remote working capabilities, detailed continuity plans, regular testing, and management reporting.
- Describes a threat-led strategic action plan prioritizing risks by impact and likelihood, with measures including technology upgrades, policy updates, extensive staff training, dedicated resources and budgets, continuous monitoring and evaluation, stakeholder communication plans, incident response protocols, and rigorous documentation and reporting.
- Strengthens supplier oversight through ESG due diligence: updated procurement policy since 2020, a Sustainability Code of Conduct for suppliers, third-party vendor assessments and ESG scorecard monitoring via EcoVadis, and KRI-based follow-up.
- Introduces an ESG Risk Management Framework (2023) defining roles across the three lines of defense, extended in 2024 to include Belfius Insurance.
- Outlines integration of ESG into financing, investing and insurance via the Transition Acceleration Policy (TAP), which sets criteria to steer activities toward low-carbon, sustainable outcomes and limit non-sustainable ones; grounded in UN Global Compact principles, with sector sensitivity screening.
- Confirms commitments to UNEP FI frameworks: Principles for Responsible Banking, Principles for Sustainable Insurance, and Principles for Responsible Investment, developed with cross-functional input (ESG, procurement, legal, communications).

nodes.title: Integration of ESG into business activities
nodes.heading: 2.4. Integration of ESG into business activities
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius is aware of the large- scale climate impact linked to financial and insurance activities, and the impact Belfius can make through its financing, investing and insurance activities.
nodes.summary:
- Physical risk exposure: Reports locations facing flood risk—55 at high risk, 44 at medium risk—totaling 20.41% of sites at elevated physical risk.
- Mitigation actions and continuity: Enterprise-wide business continuity and crisis management aligned with ISO22301 and BCI guidelines; dual-office and remote work capabilities; formal BCPs, exercises, and management reporting. A threat-prioritized action plan includes tech upgrades, policy updates, comprehensive staff training, allocated budget/resources, ongoing monitoring and evaluation, stakeholder communication, incident response protocols, and thorough documentation/reporting.
- Supplier ESG due diligence: Strengthened since 2020 via an updated Procurement Policy integrating ESG, a Supplier Sustainability Code of Conduct, and vendor assessment/monitoring with EcoVadis ESG scorecards; progress tracked through KRIs (e.g., in the QRR); reference to section 4.2.
- ESG Risk Management Framework: Established in 2023 and updated in 2024 to include Belfius Insurance; clarifies roles across the three lines of defense; see section 2.3.1.1.4.
- Integration of ESG in business activities (TAP): The Transition Acceleration Policy applies across Belfius entities and core activities with professional counterparties, setting criteria for investment, lending, and insurance to steer clients toward low-carbon, sustainable activities. It is grounded in the UN Global Compact’s 10 principles and aligned with UNEP FI PRB, PSI, and PRI; developed with input from ESG, procurement, legal, and communications.
- TAP scope, exclusions, and governance: Companies violating UN Global Compact principles, involved in controversial sectors, or breaching labor rights are excluded from most Belfius products and services (except basic banking). Exclusions from TAP include execution-only transactions, products beyond Belfius’ full control, private assets, and four illiquid run-off positions. Governance sits with the Board; the Sustainable Investment Desk designs, monitors, and implements TAP.
- Stakeholder and transparency notes: No formal external stakeholder consultation, though interests were considered; policy does not specify treatment of pollution/substances-of-concern topics. Policy available online in English, French, and Dutch. Additional details on identifying material impacts, risks, and opportunities are referenced in section 1.6.1, with “Meaningful Financing” (section 2.4.1) to detail DMA-identified material items.

nodes.summary: This section introduces Belfius’s Transition Acceleration Policy (TAP), a group-wide framework integrating ESG into investment, lending, and insurance for professional counterparties to drive a low‑carbon transition and limit non‑sustainable activities. TAP is grounded in the UN Global Compact’s 10 principles, with additional commitments to UNEP FI PRB, PSI, and PRI, and screens sensitive sectors against internal ESG criteria. Enforcement includes excluding companies violating UNGC principles (e.g., labor rights) or operating in controversial sectors from portfolios and most Belfius products and services (lending, leasing, financial markets, insurance, investments), except basic banking services; exclusions from scope include execution‑only transactions, products beyond Belfius’s full control, private assets, and four illiquid run‑off positions. Governance is overseen by the Board, with the Sustainable Investment Desk setting up, monitoring, and implementing TAP; ESG, procurement, legal, and communications were involved, while external stakeholders were not formally consulted but their interests were considered. The policy does not specify approaches to mitigating air, water, and soil pollution or managing substances of concern/SVHCs, is available online in English, French, and Dutch, and refers to section 1.6.1 for the process on identifying and assessing material impacts, risks, and opportunities.

nodes.title: Meaningful Financing
nodes.heading: 2.4.1. Meaningful Financing
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of the DMA, the following Impacts, Risks and Opportunities have been identified as material:
nodes.summary:
- Describes Belfius’ Transition Acceleration Policy (TAP), which governs investment, lending, and insurance to promote sustainable transitions and curb negative impacts, excluding companies that violate UN Global Compact principles or operate in controversial sectors from most Belfius products and services.
- Clarifies TAP scope and exceptions: applies across lending, leasing, financial markets, insurance, and investments; excludes basic banking services, execution-only transactions, investment products outside Belfius’ full control, private assets, and certain illiquid run-off positions.
- Outlines ESG/TAP governance: Board of Directors oversight; Sustainable Investment Desk designs, monitors, and implements TAP across portfolios and the investment offering.
- Notes stakeholder engagement approach and policy gaps: no specific external consultations during drafting (though interests considered); absence of explicit measures on pollution prevention/control and management of substances of concern; policy available online in English, French, and Dutch.
- Introduces the “Meaningful Financing” topic and presents material Impacts, Risks, and Opportunities (IROs) identified via the DMA, focused on downstream effects of lending and financing decisions.
- Key impacts: positive impact from financing renewable energy; potential negative impacts from financing fossil fuels, non-circular design, highly polluting sectors, water harm, ecosystem destruction, and activities with human rights or health and safety risks; role in encouraging good working conditions in the lending value chain.
- Key risks: transition risks from regulation (energy efficiency, pricing, carbon costs) affecting collateral values and borrower profitability/credit risk; physical risks from extreme weather events (e.g., flooding) impairing customers and loan performance.
- Key opportunities: new lending products supporting climate mitigation/adaptation and circular economy (including recycling), creating new revenue streams.
- References additional methodological detail on identifying and assessing material IROs in section 1.6.1 and signals the next subsection 2.4.1.1 on Advisory and Support Services.

nodes.title: Meaningful Financing - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.4.1. Meaningful Financing
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of the DMA, the following Impacts, Risks and Opportunities have been identified as material:
nodes.summary: This section outlines Belfius Bank’s material Impacts, Risks and Opportunities (IROs) for “Meaningful Financing,” identified via the DMA and focused on the downstream value chain of its lending activities. It details impacts from financing sectors supporting renewable energy versus fossil or non‑renewable energy, activities not aligned with circular design, highly polluting sectors, projects harming water availability or natural ecosystems, and exposure to human rights and health and safety risks, while also aiming to encourage good working conditions among borrowers’ workers. Key risks include regulatory changes related to climate (building energy efficiency, energy prices, carbon pricing) that could erode customers’ value and profitability, reduce property values, impair homeowners’ debt repayment, and heighten credit risk, as well as physical climate risks from extreme weather (flooding, natural disasters) impacting borrowers and Belfius’s lending portfolio. Opportunities include developing lending products that support climate mitigation and adaptation and designing offerings that advance the circular economy (including recycling), creating new revenue streams.

nodes.start_phrase: At Belfius, the guiding principle is to assist corporate clients in the intricate journey of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategy development and implementation.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on Belfius Bank’s sustainability approach within its lending value chain, detailing downstream impacts, risks, and opportunities (IRO) tied to financing decisions.
- Positive impact: financing renewable energy development; negative impacts flagged for lending to fossil fuels, non-circular models, highly polluting sectors, activities harming water resources or ecosystems, and clients with elevated human rights or health and safety risks; emphasis on promoting good working conditions in financed activities.
- Key risks: regulatory transition risks (e.g., building energy efficiency, energy prices, carbon pricing) potentially reducing asset values and client profitability, increasing credit risk; physical climate risks from extreme weather (flooding, natural disasters) affecting clients and loan performance.
- Opportunities: creation of new lending products supporting climate mitigation/adaptation and circular economy solutions (including recycling).
- Advisory and Support Services anchored in Belfius’ Climate and Environmental Policy, aimed at helping corporate clients develop and implement ESG strategies.
- Inspiration Corporate ESG Ambition: dissemination of ESG content (testimonials, legislative updates, sector impact strategies); in 2024, 2 articles published, 2 new partners onboarded, a webinar on CSRD and ESG incentives; engagement tracked via digital metrics with a goal of monthly content and topical webinars.

  - Inspiration and education: In 2024, Belfius published two ESG articles, onboarded two partners, and hosted a webinar on CSRD and ESG incentives. Engagement is tracked via LinkedIn metrics, webinar attendance, and feedback. Goal: monthly ESG content and topical webinars.

nodes.title: Responsible Mobility Solutions
nodes.heading: b) Responsible Mobility Solutions
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius offers the Energy + Car Loan, tailored for individuals looking to purchase electric or plug -in hybrid cars with CO 2 emissions of less than 50 g/km, meeting EU taxonomy criteria.
nodes.summary:
- Context and purpose: Belfius positions itself alongside public authorities to support the green transition, expanding accessible financing for energy-efficient housing and mobility, especially amid higher interest rates since 2022.

- Residential energy-efficiency financing:
  - Energy-Efficient Housing Rebates (EE Rebates): broader interest rate discounts for a wider set of energy-efficient renovations and constructions in Belgium (buildings abroad excluded), with new incentives for renewable energy adoption.
  - 30-year mortgage loan: available from July 2024 at attractive rates for energy-efficient main residences; conditions include eligibility under an EE Rebate (EPC ≤150 kWh/m²/year, new construction, or transformation), financing a main residence, and constant or decreasing instalments.
  - Flemish Renovation Credit: offered with DVV and Elantis since 2021 for deep energy renovations within five years of purchase; interest subsidy from the Flemish government depends on post-renovation energy label and loan interest rate.
  - Energy Renovation Loan (consumer loan): for smaller projects like insulation, high-efficiency glazing/boilers, heat pumps, solar panels, and energy audits.
  - 2024 volumes: EE Rebates EUR 1,296,152k (7,575 loans); 30-Year Housing Credit EUR 31,877k (131); Flemish Renovation Credit EUR 27,191k (716); Renovation loan Energy EUR 43,518k (2,429).

- Responsible mobility solutions:
  - Energy+ Car Loan: for electric or plug-in hybrid cars with CO2 <50 g/km (EU Taxonomy aligned); finance up to 120% including charger, solar panels, accessories, taxes; for new or used cars up to three years old.
  - Bike loan: finances bicycles and soft-mobility devices (e-scooters, monowheels, etc.) up to 110% including accessories, safety gear, and insurance/assistance.
  - 2024 volumes: Car loan Energy+ EUR 29,789k (1,056 loans); Bike loan EUR 4,245k (1,096).

- Corporate and public sector solutions:
  - Ambition Loans & Ambition Leasing: finance EU Taxonomy-aligned projects across real estate, mobility, energy, water, and waste (and other domains for loans).
  - 2024: launch of first socially oriented Ambition Loan to fund cybersecurity measures; further solutions planned for 2025.
  - Operational developments: charging-station leasing guidelines fully operational end-2023; updated solar panel leasing guidelines in Q3 2024; internal training rolled out from Q4 2024 to Q1 2025.
  - Tracking and reporting: monthly follow-up by product managers with efforts to streamline and automate reporting.
  - 2024 dossiers: Ambition Loans—Corporate 34, PSB 144, Business 2,020; Ambition Leasing—Corporate 1,061, PSB 9, Business 1,905.

- Upcoming content indicated: Green/Social/Sustainable Loans and Bonds (section header present, details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Green/Social/Sustainable Loans and Bonds
nodes.heading: b) Green/Social/Sustainable Loans and Bonds
nodes.start_phrase: In the context of Belfius' financing solutions, the Green Loan and/or the Social Loan are also designed to support our clients in (re)financing green and/or social projects that are fully aligned with all categories and conditions mentioned in the European Taxonomy, thereby aligning with Europe's vision and its Green Deal to achieve a Zero Emission policy by 2050.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Belfius Bank’s 2024 sustainability-driven financing and mobility offerings for individuals, corporates, and the public sector, with performance metrics and governance of these products.

- Retail responsible mobility:
  - Energy+ Car Loan: For electric or plug-in hybrids emitting <50 g CO2/km, EU Taxonomy-aligned; financing up to 120% of purchase price including charging stations, solar panels, accessories, registration tax; for new or used (≤3 years) vehicles.
  - Bike Loan: Financing for bicycles and soft-mobility devices (e-scooters, monowheels, Segways, etc.) up to 110% of purchase price, including accessories, safety gear, and portions of insurance/assistance.
  - 2024 volumes: Car Loan Energy+ EUR 29,789k across 1,056 loans; Bike Loan EUR 4,245k across 1,096 loans.

- Corporate and Public Sector solutions:
  - Ambition Loans & Ambition Leasing: Financing for environmentally positive projects aligned with EU Taxonomy (real estate, mobility, energy, water/waste). First socially oriented Ambition Loan launched in 2024 for cybersecurity protection; further solutions planned for 2025. Charging-station leasing guidelines fully operational end-2023; updated solar panel leasing guidelines in Q3 2024; internal training rolling out Q4 2024–Q1 2025. Monthly KPI tracking with reporting automation in progress.
  - 2024 dossiers: Ambition Loans—Corporate 34, PSB 144, Business 2,020; Ambition Leasing—Corporate 1,061, PSB 9, Business 1,905.

- Green/Social/Sustainable Loans and Bonds:
  - Loans: Support (re)financing of green/social projects fully aligned with EU Taxonomy; Social Loan targets projects with positive social impact; actions are client-specific and ad hoc; advisory available via Financial Markets for client financing frameworks.
  - Bonds: Client-driven green/social bond issuance within a certified framework (SPO required) and detailed use-of-proceeds reporting; quarterly tracking of transactions and volumes split by PSB/Corporate.
  - 2024 issuance: EUR 2,459 million in Green/Social/Sustainable Bonds.

- Sustainability-Linked Loans/Bonds (SLL/SLB):
  - Instruments with pricing linked to ESG/KPI performance aligned with credible frameworks (e.g., Paris Agreement); KPIs must be relevant, ambitious, and verifiable.
  - Monthly monitoring covers confirmed LMA-aligned SLLs and facilities with provisions to set KPIs for future conversion; tracked metrics include number of dossiers, volumes, and margins.
  - 2024 outcomes: 7 new SLL facilities totaling EUR 366 million; 4 prior facilities converted to SLLs after KPI/target agreement.

- Comprehensive mobility for companies:
  - Car financing via investment credit/leasing (with optional services) to green fleets.
  - Bicycle leasing with services via Cyclis to facilitate employee commuting.
  - Integrated protection through insurance within leasing packages.

nodes.title: Sustainability Linked Loans (SLL) and Bonds (SLB)
nodes.heading: c) Sustainability Linked Loans (SLL) and Bonds (SLB)
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius offers a financing solution in the form of a bond or credit designed for general corporate purposes, with a unique feature where the interest rate is tied to the issuer's achievement of sustainable development or ESG criteria objectives, known as Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
nodes.summary:
- Belfius’ sustainable financing offering includes Green Loans and Social Loans to (re)finance projects fully aligned with the EU Taxonomy, supporting the EU Green Deal’s 2050 net-zero goals; Social Loans target projects with positive social impact for specific groups.
- Actions are tailored and conducted ad hoc due to client-specific needs; clients can be supported by Belfius Financial Markets experts to develop Green/Social/Sustainable Financing Frameworks, typically following in-depth client–banker discussions rather than proactive outreach.
- Green/Social/Sustainable Bonds: use-of-proceeds bonds for green and/or social projects, anchored in a client financing framework, requiring a Second Party Opinion and detailed allocation reporting. Demand is client-driven; the team engages once the concept is defined. Quarterly metrics (split PSB vs Corporate) track number of transactions and issuance volumes; 2024 issuance totaled EUR 2,459 million.
- Sustainability-Linked Loans and Bonds: general corporate financing with pricing linked to achievement of material, verifiable, and ambitious ESG KPIs aligned with frameworks like the Paris Agreement, documented in financing terms or a sustainability-linked framework. Monthly monitoring distinguishes LMA-aligned confirmed SLLs from facilities with provisions to set KPIs for future conversion; metrics include number of dossiers, total volume, and average margin (bps). In 2024, 7 new SLLs totaling EUR 366 million were originated and 4 existing facilities were converted to SLLs.
- Comprehensive Mobility Solutions for companies and employees: greener fleet financing via investment credit or leasing; bicycle leasing with services through Cyclis; and insurance protection integrated into leasing packages.

nodes.title: Comprehensive Mobility Solutions
nodes.heading: d) Comprehensive Mobility Solutions
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius is committed to providing concrete and responsible mobility solutions to meet the evolving needs of companies and their employees.
nodes.summary:
- Focus area: Belfius Bank’s sustainable financing and mobility/infrastructure solutions within the 2024 Sustainability Statement, highlighting client-driven offerings, governance, and performance metrics.

- Green/Social Loans:
  - Purpose: (Re)finance green and/or social projects fully aligned with the EU Taxonomy and the EU Green Deal (Net Zero by 2050). Social Loans target positive social impacts for specific groups.
  - Delivery model: Ad hoc, tailored to client needs; support from Belfius Financial Markets for clients developing Green/Social/Sustainable Financing Frameworks; services are not proactively marketed but arise from in-depth client discussions.

- Green/Social/Sustainable Bonds:
  - Structure: Financing via bonds for ecological transition and/or social impact projects, included in a client’s sustainable financing framework; requires Second Party Opinion and detailed use-of-proceeds reporting.
  - Process: Demand is client-driven; Belfius team engages once the bond concept is well-defined, with bankers initiating contact.
  - Monitoring: Quarterly tracking by product managers, split between PSB and Corporate; metrics include number of transactions and issuance volumes.
  - 2024 result: EUR 2,459 million in Green/Social/Sustainable bond issuance.

- Sustainability-Linked Loans and Bonds (SLL/SLB):
  - Feature: Interest margin linked to achievement of ESG KPIs aligned with frameworks like the Paris Agreement; KPIs must be relevant, consistent, verifiable, and ambitious; embedded in financing docs or a sustainability-linked framework.
  - Monitoring: Monthly tracking; operational split between LMA-aligned confirmed SLLs and facilities with provisions to set KPIs/targets for future SLL conversion. Metrics include number of dossiers, volumes, and average margin (bps).
  - 2024 result: 7 new SLL facilities totaling EUR 366 million; 4 existing facilities converted to SLL after KPI/target agreement.

- Comprehensive Mobility Solutions:
  - Offerings: 
    - Cars: Investment credit or leasing (with/without services) to green fleets.
    - Bike: Bicycle leasing via Cyclis.
    - Protection: Insurance bundled with leasing.
    - Electrification: Charging solutions for employees/sites via CenEnergy.
    - MaaS: Skipr app aggregating mobility options.
    - Advisory: Tailored transition support.
  - 2024 actions: Launched on-site charging with CenEnergy (press release; mailing to PSB/Corporate); participated in Mobility Tomorrow with subsidiaries/partners and released a mobility podcast.
  - Metrics (31/12/2024):
    - Operational car leasing: Electric 8,417 (28%); Plug-in hybrid 7,077 (24%); Hydrogen 0 (0%).
    - Bicycle leases: 991 contracts.
    - Charging stations (linked to car leasing): 277.
    - MaaS subscriptions: 417.
  - Target: Reduce Belfius Auto Lease fleet CO2 emissions by 50% by 2025 vs 2019.

- Energy-efficient infrastructure:
  - SBRS (Smart Building & Renovation Solution): End-to-end real estate project support from audits to delivery.
  - SBRS Energy: Focused on energy renovation (HVAC, electricity, lighting, building envelope) and energy sharing.
  - 2024 development: Commercial launch of an energy sharing solution with WeSmart for local authorities, hospitals, schools, and universities; recognized as innovative in the Belgian market.
  - Go-to-market: Dedicated sales team for Walloon and Flemish PSB clients with a proactive regional approach.
  - Governance/monitoring: Monthly reporting to ManCo on number of files, project and credit volumes, and fees. Energy sharing pipeline includes ~10 feasibility studies; no finalized sales yet.

nodes.title: Meaningful Investing
nodes.heading: 2.4.2. Meaningful Investing
nodes.start_phrase: Meaningful investing is the cornerstone of Belfius’ investment strategy.
nodes.summary:
- Reports SBRS and SBRS Energy production volumes: EUR 318m in 2023 and EUR 307m in 2024; about 50% of projects funded each year (EUR 161m in 2023; EUR 155m expected in 2024). 2024 energy sharing projects are exploratory with no specific production targets; information on outstanding amounts and new projects is available.
- Describes renewable energy syndicated loans, where multiple institutions participate and one leads (e.g., wind farms). Emissions reductions are expected primarily via customers’ own reductions, with expectations that customers comply with environmental laws and disclose required impacts.
- Presents “Meaningful Investing” as Belfius’ core investment approach, aiming for both financial and societal returns and integrating ESG factors to better assess risks and opportunities.
- Summarizes material Impacts, Risks, and Opportunities (IROs) identified via the DMA for the downstream value chain:
  - Positive impacts from investing in renewables, circular economy, water and marine protection, biodiversity/forest preservation, worker health and safety, and human rights.
  - Negative impacts from investments in fossil-based energy, non-circular practices, highly polluting sectors, activities harming water and ecosystems, and those linked to accidents or discrimination.
  - Risks from climate-related regulation (e.g., energy efficiency, pricing, carbon costs) and from extreme weather events affecting investee value and profitability.
  - Opportunities to develop products supporting climate mitigation/adaptation and circular economy, creating new revenue streams.
- Outlines Responsible Investment methods at Belfius Asset Management (Belfius AM):
  - A formal Responsible Investment Policy covering setup, governance, application, exclusion criteria, ESG integration, thematic investing, risk management, and due diligence for adverse impacts.
  - Governance by the Belfius AM management committee, with a Responsible Investing Committee overseeing implementation and methodologies.
  - Scope spans all assets managed (with asset-class-specific exceptions), including explicit exclusions (e.g., tobacco, gambling) and alignment with UN Global Compact principles.
  - Commitment to transparency via publicly available policies and regular reporting, including an annual active ownership report.
  - Use of exclusions through the TAP to screen out ineligible sectors, companies, or governments based on legal, norms-based, or sustainability considerations.

nodes.title: Meaningful Investing - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.4.2. Meaningful Investing
nodes.start_phrase: Meaningful investing is the cornerstone of Belfius’ investment strategy.
nodes.summary: This section introduces Belfius Bank’s Meaningful Investing as the cornerstone of its investment strategy, emphasizing a fiduciary duty to deliver both financial and societal returns and to integrate ESG factors into the investment process. Following the DMA, a downstream value-chain IRO table identifies material impacts: positive (prioritizing renewable energy; circular design and recycling; protecting water and marine resources; supporting biodiversity, forests, and ecosystems; promoting worker health, safety, and good working conditions; protecting human rights) and negative (financing fossil-based energy; non-circular practices; highly polluting activities; harm to water preservation; destruction of ecosystems; sectors with high accident/illness risk; discrimination and exclusion). It also highlights risks from climate-related regulation (e.g., energy efficiency, prices, carbon pricing) and extreme weather/natural disasters that may impair customers’ value and Belfius’s financials, and opportunities to create products for climate mitigation/adaptation and the circular economy that generate new revenue streams.

nodes.title: Responsible investments methods
nodes.heading: 2.4.2.1. Responsible investments methods
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius fully recognizes its role as an investor and its ability to use the capital invested on behalf of clients to generate financial returns and create beneficial change.
nodes.summary:
- Identifies downstream opportunities to create new revenue by developing investment products that support climate mitigation/adaptation and the circular economy (including recycling).
- Describes Belfius Asset Management’s Responsible Investment Policy as a framework for the setup, governance, and execution of responsible investing across its portfolios.
- Specifies governance: the Belfius AM management committee is accountable for policy implementation, with a Responsible Investing Committee validating implementation and methodologies.
- States the investment philosophy to deliver both financial and societal returns as part of fiduciary duty, using data-driven ESG integration to better assess risks and opportunities.
- Details policy components: methods, governance, application, exclusion criteria, ESG integration, thematic investments, risk management, and due diligence to assess negative impacts.
- Confirms scope covers all assets managed by Belfius AM, with possible asset-class-specific exceptions; explicitly excludes sectors with significant negative impacts (e.g., tobacco, gambling) via the TAP framework.
- Aligns with the UN Global Compact principles and commits to transparency through stakeholder updates, published policies, and an annual active ownership report.
- Emphasizes that sustainability is multi-dimensional and requires varied ESG methods, including exclusions based on legal, norms-based, or sustainability considerations.

nodes.title: Responsible investments methods - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.4.2.1. Responsible investments methods
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius fully recognizes its role as an investor and its ability to use the capital invested on behalf of clients to generate financial returns and create beneficial change.
nodes.summary: This introduction outlines Belfius Asset Management’s Responsible Investment Policy, establishing the framework, scope, and governance for integrating ESG across all managed assets (with possible asset class or structure-based exceptions). The Management Committee holds ultimate accountability, while the Responsible Investing Committee validates implementation and methodologies. The policy aims to deliver both financial and societal returns as part of fiduciary duty, emphasizes systematic, data-driven ESG incorporation to assess risks and opportunities, and covers methods, governance, application, exclusion criteria, ESG integration, thematic investment, risk management, and due diligence for negative impacts. It explicitly excludes sectors with significant harm, such as tobacco and gambling, aligns with the UN Global Compact principles, and commits to transparency via stakeholder updates, detailed online policies, comprehensive disclosures, and an annual active ownership report.

nodes.title: Exclusions
nodes.heading: Exclusions
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius excludes certain economic activities on sustainability grounds through its TAP (see section 2.4.) .
nodes.summary:
- Highlights new business opportunities from climate mitigation/adaptation solutions and circular-economy products that can create downstream revenue for Belfius’s investing activities.
- Describes Belfius Asset Management’s Responsible Investment Policy: purpose, scope, and governance (Management Committee oversight; Responsible Investing Committee for implementation and methodologies).
- Emphasizes dual objective of financial and societal returns, data-driven ESG integration, and alignment with UN Global Compact; commits to transparency via published policies and an annual active ownership report.
- Outlines core responsible investment methods, notably exclusions and active ownership (engagement and proxy voting).
- Details exclusions via the Transition Acceleration Policy (TAP): periodic monitoring of issuer compliance; Q4 2024 shows 8.61% of issuers non-compliant; application across direct investments, delegated managers, and rigorous screening of third-party funds.
- Summarizes 2024 TAP updates targeting energy sector: from 1 Aug 2024 exclusion of all coal extraction firms and companies with coal expansion plans; full coal exclusion by 2030; exclusion of unconventional oil and gas (e.g., shale, tar sands, arctic/deepwater drilling, coalbed methane, extra heavy oil).
- Notes assessment of Principal Adverse Impacts (PAIs) and alignment of TAP exclusions with certain PAIs; clarifies no outcome targets for exclusions since they primarily mitigate ESG risk.
- Explains active ownership approach: engagement to improve ESG disclosure and practices; Proxy Voting Policy guiding votes in beneficiaries’ best interests, supporting shareholder rights, board objectivity, transparency, and long-term value; policy applies to internally managed funds with direct equity holdings; voting at AGMs/EGMs on these holdings in 2024.

nodes.title: Active Ownership: Engagement & Proxy Voting
nodes.heading: Active Ownership: Engagement & Proxy Voting
nodes.start_phrase: Active ownership refers to creating beneficial change by engaging with the management of investee companies and by voting at shareholder meetings of listed equities.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of Belfius Asset Management’s (Belfius AM) responsible investment framework, focusing on the Transition Acceleration Policy (TAP), active ownership (engagement and proxy voting), ESG integration, sustainable and thematic investing, and additional ESG policies (notably climate).
- TAP monitoring and enforcement:
  - Periodic assessment of TAP compliance across the investment universe; in Q4 2024, 8.61% of issuers were non-TAP-compliant.
  - Exclusion/divestment of non-TAP-compliant issuers across direct investments, private mandates, managed funds, and insurance-based products; delegated managers required to adhere to TAP; rigorous ESG-inclusive selection and ongoing screening of third-party funds.
  - January 2024 TAP update: from 1 Aug 2024, exclusion of all coal extraction companies and companies with coal mining/power expansion plans; by 2030, exclusion of all coal companies; exclusion of unconventional oil and gas (e.g., shale, tar sands, arctic, deepwater, coalbed methane, extra heavy oil).
  - Alignment of TAP exclusions with Principal Adverse Impacts (PAIs); disclosure via annual PAI statement; no outcome targets for exclusions since policy is risk-mitigation oriented.
- Active ownership:
  - Proxy voting policy for internally managed equity funds; principles emphasize equal shareholder rights, robust and independent boards, performance-aligned and transparent remuneration, auditor independence/rotation, and ESG transparency; supportive of material ESG shareholder proposals.
  - Voting approach: Belfius AM votes on direct equity holdings in internally managed funds; encourages underlying managers to vote in funds of funds; requires voting by delegated managers; no voting on single-line holdings in private portfolio management, while external fund managers may vote.
  - Reporting of voting activity (volumes, for/against rates, category breakdown) and publication of an annual Active Ownership report.
  - Engagement policy covering direct company engagement and oversight of external managers; expectations for external managers include formal engagement policies, addressing PAIs, structural commitments for Article 8/9 products, exercising voting rights, and public reporting of activities/results.
  - Policy alignment with SRD II, SFDR, TCFD, and UN SDG 8; annual transparency commitments; ongoing review of active ownership strategy with no specific targets set yet; tracking of engagement metrics (share of engagements, topics, and types).
- ESG integration:
  - Systematic incorporation of ESG factors into financial analysis tailored by fund/mandate.
  - Use of social and ESG questionnaires, ESG ratings, and stringent ESG due diligence in third-party fund selection; only funds with strong ESG credentials considered.
- Sustainable investments (SFDR):
  - Definition consistent with SFDR; sustainable investments primarily within Article 8 and 9 funds.
  - Group target: 100% of production in meaningful Article 8/9 investments by 2025; achievement at 96% in FY2024.
- Thematic investing:
  - Funds with binding environmental/social criteria linked to SDGs; focus on solutions for cleaner, safer, smarter mobility and climate change mitigation.
- Additional ESG policies, especially Climate policy:
  - Strategy centered on climate transition; reiterates TAP coal phase-out by 2030 and exclusion of coal expansion from Aug 2024; exclusion of unconventional oil & gas.
  - Establishes stringent criteria for conventional oil & gas companies and electricity producers.
  - Broad scope covering funds of funds, delegated funds, direct line-managed funds, and private portfolio management.

nodes.title: ESG Integration
nodes.heading: ESG Integration
nodes.start_phrase: ESG integration involves incorporating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into financial analysis, valuation, and decision -making processes in a systematic and documented manner.
nodes.summary:
- Active ownership: Annual publication of engagement and proxy voting activities; guided by Belfius AM Engagement and Proxy Voting Policies.
- ESG integration: Systematic inclusion of environmental, social, and governance factors in analysis and decisions, tailored by fund/mandate. Tools include social questionnaires (e.g., turnover, training, gender pay gap), use of ESG ratings by portfolio managers, and a fund selection process that screens third-party funds via detailed ESG questionnaires, investing only in those with strong ESG credentials.
- Sustainable investments (SFDR): Definition per SFDR; primarily within Article 8 and 9 funds. Group target of 100% production in meaningful investments (SFDR Art. 8 & 9) by 2025 across mutual funds, My Portfolio, pension funds, and investment-insurance products; achieved 96% in FY2024.
- Thematic investing: Funds with binding environmental or social criteria linked to SDGs, focusing on themes like cleaner, safer, smarter mobility and climate change mitigation leadership.
- Additional ESG policies: Climate policy focused on transition, including a Thermal Asset Phase-out (TAP) to eliminate coal investments by 2030 and exclude companies planning coal expansion from August 2024. Broad scope across funds and portfolio management. Exclusions extend to unconventional oil & gas, with stringent criteria for conventional oil & gas and electricity producers.

nodes.title: Sustainable Investments
nodes.heading: Sustainable Investments
nodes.start_phrase: As defined by SFDR, sustainable Investments refer to investments in an economic activity that contributes to an environmental objective, or investments in an economic activity that contributes to a social objective, provided that such investments do not significantly harm any of those objectives and that the investee companies follow good governance practices, in particular with respect to sound management structures, employee relations, remuneration of staff and tax compliance.
nodes.summary:
- The document outlines Belfius AM’s active ownership practices, including annual publication of engagement and voting activities and references to its Engagement and Proxy Voting Policies.
- It explains ESG integration as a systematic, documented part of financial analysis for actively managed portfolios, tailored by fund/mandate objectives. Tools include social questionnaires (e.g., turnover, training, gender pay gap), the use of ESG ratings by portfolio managers, and a fund selection process that screens third-party funds via detailed ESG questionnaires, admitting only those with strong ESG credentials.
- It defines Sustainable Investments under SFDR, noting that such investments are typically in Article 8 and 9 funds. Belfius targets 100% of production in SFDR Art. 8 & 9 products (mutual funds, My Portfolio, pension funds, investment-insurance) by 2025, with 96% achieved in FY2024.
- It describes thematic investing in long-term trends tied to SDGs, with funds applying binding environmental or social criteria and focusing on areas like cleaner, safer, smarter mobility and climate change mitigation leadership.
- It presents additional ESG policies, notably a Climate Policy that integrates ESG into decision-making and includes a phase-out of coal-related investments by 2030, exclusion of companies planning coal expansion from August 2024, applicability across funds of funds, delegated and direct line-managed funds, and private portfolio management, exclusions for unconventional oil & gas, and strict criteria for conventional oil & gas companies and electricity producers.

nodes.title: Thematic Investing
nodes.heading: Thematic Investing
nodes.start_phrase: Thematic investing refers to investing in themes related to new and/or long -term trends.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines Belfius AM’s active ownership approach, noting annual publication of engagement and voting activities and referencing Engagement and Proxy Voting Policies.
- Defines ESG integration and describes its application in actively managed portfolios, tailored per fund/mandate, including use of social questionnaires, ESG ratings, and a rigorous third-party fund selection process focused on strong ESG credentials.
- Explains SFDR-aligned sustainable investments, highlighting that Article 8 and 9 products house these investments; Belfius Group targets 100% production in such products by 2025 across key investment solutions, reaching 96% in FY2024.
- Describes thematic investing aligned with long-term sustainability trends and SDGs, with funds applying binding environmental or social criteria and focusing on areas such as cleaner, safer, smarter mobility and climate change mitigation leadership.
- Details additional ESG policies, especially Belfius AM’s Climate Policy: integrates ESG into investment decisions; sets a coal exit by 2030 and excludes companies planning coal expansion from August 2024; applies across funds and portfolio management; restricts unconventional oil & gas and imposes stringent criteria for conventional oil & gas and electricity producers.

nodes.title: Additional ESG policies
nodes.heading: 2.4.2.2. Additional ESG policies
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius AM’s commitment is also reflected in its concrete directives:
nodes.summary:
- Belfius AM reports annually on engagement and proxy voting in an Active Ownership report and follows dedicated Engagement and Proxy Voting Policies.
- ESG integration is embedded in investment analysis and decision-making, customized by fund/mandate. Methods include social questionnaires (e.g., turnover, training, gender pay gap), use of ESG ratings by portfolio managers, and a fund selection process that screens third-party funds via detailed ESG questionnaires, investing only in managers with strong ESG credentials.
- Sustainable investments are defined per SFDR and are primarily implemented in Article 8 and 9 funds. Belfius Group targets 100% of product “production” in SFDR Art. 8/9 by 2025 across mutual funds, My Portfolio, pension funds, and investment-insurance products; achievement stands at 96% in FY2024.
- Thematic investing focuses on long-term sustainability trends, with funds applying binding environmental or social criteria aligned to SDGs, investing in areas like cleaner, safer, smarter mobility and climate change mitigation leadership.
- Additional ESG policies include a comprehensive Climate Policy prioritizing transition, integrating ESG into decisions, and a Transition Acceleration Plan to eliminate coal investments by 2030 and exclude companies planning coal expansion from August 2024. The policy spans funds of funds, delegated and direct mandates, and private portfolio management, excludes unconventional oil & gas, and sets strict criteria for conventional oil & gas and electricity producers.

nodes.summary:
Additional ESG policies

nodes.title: Belfius AM’s Climate policy
nodes.heading: Belfius AM’s Climate policy
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius AM’s Climate policy is cent red on a strategic approach to addressing climate -related challenges within the investment sphere, emphasizing the transition towards a sustainable economy.
nodes.summary:
- Describes Belfius AM’s active ownership, noting annual publication of engagement and proxy voting activities and reference policies.
- Explains ESG integration as a systematic, documented process tailored by fund/mandate, using tools like social questionnaires (e.g., turnover, training, gender pay gap), ESG ratings, and rigorous third-party fund due diligence to select managers with strong ESG credentials.
- Defines sustainable investments per SFDR and notes they are concentrated in Article 8 and 9 funds; highlights Belfius Group’s target of 100% production in Article 8/9 products by 2025 (mutual funds, My Portfolio, pension, and investment-insurance), with 96% achieved in FY2024.
- Outlines thematic investing in SDG-linked funds with binding environmental or social criteria, focusing on cleaner, safer, smarter mobility and climate change mitigation leaders.
- Details additional ESG policies:
  - Climate policy: transition-focused; aims to eliminate coal investments by 2030 and exclude companies planning coal expansion from August 2024; covers all fund types; excludes coal and unconventional oil & gas; imposes strict criteria for conventional oil & gas and power producers; aligned with UN Global Compact and TCFD; shaped by stakeholder input.
  - Pollution & Waste policy: targets pollution reduction and single-use plastics; applies to all funds; engages investees and external managers; monitors negative impact indicators.
  - Water Use policy: integrates water sustainability across all funds; emphasizes engagement, monitoring, and encouraging managers to assess water impacts.
  - Biodiversity policy: addresses drivers of biodiversity loss in sectors like forestry, agriculture, fishing, mining, and land grabbing; excludes deforestation-linked firms unless meeting TAP standards; encourages external managers’ biodiversity policies; references human rights norms and UN Global Compact; considers diverse stakeholders.
  - Gender & Diversity policy: promotes diversity and equality across all funds with stakeholder engagement and regular monitoring.
- Notes governance and transparency: policies are implemented by Belfius AM’s Management Board and published on its website; effectiveness metrics are not externally validated beyond the assurance provider.

nodes.title: Belfius Green and Social Bonds
nodes.heading: 2.4.2.3 . Belfius Green and Social Bonds
nodes.start_phrase: Well aware of the crucial role played by the financial sector in ensuring a more sustainable future, Belfius aims to be meaningful and inspiring through its core businesses – not only for its customers, but also for the Belgian society as a whole.
nodes.summary:
- The section outlines Belfius Bank’s sustainability financing via Green and Social Bonds within its 2024 Annual Report.
- Frameworks:
  - Green Bond Framework (GBF) published in May 2021, aligned with ICMA Green Bond Principles.
  - Social Bond Framework (SBF) published in March 2024, aligned with ICMA Social Bond Principles.
  - Both frameworks reviewed by an independent Second Party Opinion provider; no specific issuance targets set.
- 2024 issuances:
  - EUR 750 million in Green Bonds to (re)finance eligible green loans and investments supporting a low-carbon, climate‑resilient transition.
  - EUR 575 million in Social Bonds to (re)finance eligible social loans and investments addressing social issues and promoting positive social outcomes, including for target populations.
- Reporting and assurance:
  - Annual allocation reports covering outstanding amounts, portfolio breakdown by eligible category, and any unallocated balances.
  - Impact reporting on key KPIs: environmental impact for Green Bonds and positive social impact for Social Bonds.
  - Reports subject to external Limited Assurance by an auditor.
- Governance:
  - A Green & Social Bond Committee oversees evaluation and selection of eligible assets and approves allocation and impact reports.
- Additional resources:
  - Full frameworks, eligible asset criteria, KPIs, annual reports, governance details, Second Party Opinion, and Limited Assurance Reports available at https://www.belfius.be/about-us/en/investors/debt-issuance/green-social-bonds.
- The next subsection (2.4.3 Meaningful Insurance) indicates that, following the DMA, material impacts, risks, and opportunities have been identified (details not included in this excerpt).

nodes.title: Meaningful Insurance
nodes.heading: 2.4.3. Meaningful Insurance
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of the DMA, the following Impacts, Risks and Opportunities have been identified as material:
nodes.summary:
- Belfius’ Green and Social Bond strategy:
  - Green Bond Framework (2021) aligned with ICMA Green Bond Principles; Social Bond Framework (2024) aligned with ICMA Social Bond Principles; both reviewed by an independent Second Party Opinion provider.
  - 2024 issuance: EUR 750 million in Green Bonds and EUR 575 million in Social Bonds; no specific issuance targets set.
  - Purpose: (re)finance eligible green and social assets, enhance transparency on environmental and social benefits.
  - Reporting: annual allocation and impact reports covering outstanding amounts, portfolio breakdown by category, unallocated proceeds, and KPIs on environmental and social outcomes; external Limited Assurance provided.
  - Governance: a Green & Social Bond Committee evaluates/ selects eligible assets and approves allocation and impact reports; detailed frameworks, eligible assets, KPIs, SPOs and assurance reports available on Belfius’ investor website.

- Meaningful Insurance: material impacts, risks and opportunities (downstream) identified via DMA:
  - Impacts: supporting climate transition and biodiversity; incentivizing adaptation; potential exposure to fossil-fuel activities, ecosystem destruction, human rights, and health and safety risks; promoting good working conditions.
  - Risks: mispricing non-life insurance for climate-related events; financial impacts from customer losses due to natural disasters.
  - Opportunities: new products for climate mitigation/adaptation and circular-economy solutions.

- Role of Belfius Insurance:
  - Non-life: protection against life hazards including climate-related catastrophes.
  - Life: addressing healthcare and pension needs to build societal resilience.
  - Investments: financing essential infrastructure; active engagement with investees, suppliers and customers to encourage sustainable behavior.

- Meaningful Insurance Journey and product lifecycle:
  - ESG embedded across product management and customer servicing; policies integrate climate change and biodiversity; circular economy viewed as a strategic opportunity.

- Product management and pricing:
  - Climate considerations integrated into property and mobility insurance; measurement of EU Taxonomy-aligned Green Non-Life Premium.
  - ESG integrated in product approval processes overseen by the Management Board; Product Oversight and Governance to ensure customer fit and value for money under IDD.
  - Pricing Policy Non-Life aligns with profitability, risk appetite and climate risk, with continuous monitoring and regulatory compliance.

- Mobility initiatives:
  - Three-pronged approach: avoid, reduce, replace emissions.
  - Products encouraging sustainable mobility: All Risk Bicycle Insurance (award-winning, comprehensive coverage) and Complementary Bicycle Assistance, promoting cycling adoption.

nodes.title: Meaningful Insurance - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.4.3. Meaningful Insurance
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of the DMA, the following Impacts, Risks and Opportunities have been identified as material:
nodes.summary: This section introduces Belfius Insurance’s “Meaningful Insurance” topic, listing DMA-identified material Impacts, Risks and Opportunities focused on the downstream value chain. Impacts include developing insurance and (re)insurance that support the climate transition, climate adaptation, biodiversity, and good working conditions, alongside potential negative impacts from insuring fossil fuel-based energy, activities harming ecosystems, and sectors with elevated human rights or health and safety risks. Key risks are mispricing non-life products by not factoring climate events and financial losses from customers’ reduced value/profitability due to floods and other natural disasters. Opportunities include new revenue from products enabling climate mitigation/adaptation and circular economy (e.g., recycling). The section adds that non-life products protect against climate-related catastrophes, life insurance addresses healthcare and pensions to bolster a resilient Belgian society, investment activities advance essential infrastructure, and the company engages investees, suppliers, and customers to encourage sustainable behaviors.

nodes.title: Meaningful Insurance Journey
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.1 Meaningful Insurance Journey
nodes.start_phrase: To address current and future environmental and social challenges, Belfius Insurance encourages virtuous behaviour by incorporating environmental parameters into its product offerings throughout its product lifecycle.
nodes.summary:
- Belfius Insurance embeds ESG principles across the entire insurance journey, integrating key environmental challenges—especially climate change and biodiversity—into policies. While there is no standalone circular economy policy, it is seen as a strategic opportunity aligned with broader environmental goals.
- Product Management & Pricing: Products are tailored to protect clients from natural catastrophes and evolving environmental risks. Climate and environmental commitments are anchored in Belfius’ CEP, with measurement of EU Taxonomy–aligned non-life premiums (“Green Non-Life Premium”). ESG is integrated into the Approval Process Policy, overseen by the Management Board with multidisciplinary risk assessments. The Product Oversight and Governance Policy (under IDD, excluding large risks) ensures products meet customer needs, including sustainability objectives, and deliver value for money. The Non-Life Pricing Policy, approved by the Management Board, aligns with risk appetite including climate risk, and requires continuous pricing monitoring within regulatory guidelines.
- Mobility: A three-pronged decarbonization approach—avoid, reduce, replace—guides initiatives. Belfius facilitates shifts to sustainable mobility via a market-leading All Risk Bicycle Insurance (covering theft, damage, breakdowns, and flat batteries for non-motorized vehicles up to 25 km/h), awarded Decavi prizes in 2022, 2023, and 2024. Complementary bicycle assistance within personal assistance products encourages cycling as a sustainable transport mode.

nodes.title: Product Management & Pricing
nodes.heading: 2.4.3.1.1. Product Management & Pricing
nodes.start_phrase: Belfius Insurance aims to address the evolving needs of its clients, particularly in the face of increasing environmental challenges.
nodes.summary:
- Section from Belfius Bank’s 2024 Annual Report (Sustainability Statement) detailing Belfius Insurance’s “Meaningful Insurance Journey,” i.e., how ESG is embedded across the insurance product lifecycle—from product design and approval to pricing and customer service.
- Focus on integrating environmental challenges, notably Climate Change and Biodiversity, into policies; circular economy lacks a dedicated policy but is seen as a strategic opportunity.
- Product Management & Pricing: tailoring offerings to protect clients from natural catastrophes and evolving environmental risks; alignment with a Climate & Environment Policy to proactively manage climate impacts on property and mobility insurance.
- Measurement of EU Taxonomy-aligned non-life premiums via the Green Non-Life Premium indicator.
