nodes.start_phrase: As at 31 December 2024, a total 89% of Group employees were covered by applicable national collective bargaining agreements, with 100% of Italian employees covered.
nodes.summary:
- Describes Intesa Sanpaolo’s structured labour relations and social dialogue framework, including a Labour Relations Protocol, frequent meetings with trade unions at group and local levels, and bilateral company/union bodies focused on equal opportunities, welfare, safety and sustainability.
- Notes creation (23 Oct 2024) of a new bilateral body to monitor impacts of technological innovation and digitalisation on bank branches, with findings reported at the group negotiating table.
- Outlines governance responsibilities: the Chief People & Culture Officer’s Governance Area oversees labour and remuneration policies; the Relations with Workers’ Representatives and Welfare unit manages operational dialogue.
- Details remuneration policies:
  - Application of Italy’s National Collective Bargaining Agreement (NCBA) and enterprise-level bargaining for pay structures, career paths, and benefits; compliance with local CBAs or laws abroad, with standard conditions across countries except improved terms for top management.
  - Group-wide short-term incentive plan (PVR) originating in 2015; 2024 PVR includes:
    - Base Bonus by professional profile (1,150–2,950 euro, with an extra quota for incomes up to 39,000 euro).
    - Excellence Bonus tied to outstanding individual and team performance, with a dedicated quota for insurance sales network staff.
    - Inclusion of employees on long absences (including parental leave) and option to convert bonuses into welfare services for tax efficiency.
  - Outcome of the 23 Nov 2023 NCBA renegotiation: average monthly pay rise of 435 euro, phased (250 from 1 Jul 2023; 100 from 1 Sep 2024; 50 from 1 Jun 2025; 35 from 1 Mar 2026).
  - Pay review guidelines emphasize market benchmarks, performance, gender equality, and equal pay for equal work to support talent attraction and retention.
- Presents coverage metrics:
  - 89% of Group employees covered by collective bargaining; 100% coverage in Italy.
  - 76% of Italian employees are union members.
  - No European Works Council/SE/SCE Works Council agreements in place.
- Affirms commitment to adequate wages: all employees paid at least the legal/collectively agreed minimum in each country, aligned with EU Directive 2022/2041 in the EEA and relevant standards outside the EEA.
- Describes engagement processes: weekly meetings at Group Delegation level, ad hoc Consultation Committee for dispute resolution, quarterly committees (Welfare/Safety/Sustainable Development; Business Policy & Corporate Climate), and quarterly local meetings; over 30 agreements concluded in 2024.
- Explains grievance and remediation channels: Code of Ethics inbox and 24/7 whistleblowing system for employees and third parties with confidentiality and non-retaliation; collective bargaining mechanisms for assessing infringements, escalation to legal processes where laws are breached, and the Consultation Committee for local dispute resolution.

nodes.title: Metrics on adequate wages
nodes.heading: 4.1.5.4 Metrics on adequate wages
nodes.start_phrase: The Group is committed to guaranteeing an adequate wage for all its employees.
nodes.summary:
- Focuses on employee relations within the Group in the Consolidated Sustainability Statement, with Italy identified as the only country where the workforce is significant.
- Coverage rates: in Italy, 100% of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements and approximately 76% by workplace representation/social dialogue structures.
- Confirms there are no agreements in place for European Works Council (EWC), Societas Europaea (SE) Works Council, or Societas Cooperativa Europaea (SCE) Works Council representation.
- States all employees receive an “adequate minimum wage,” defined by national law or collective bargaining agreements; references EU Directive 2022/2041 for EEA countries and equivalent standards outside the EEA ensuring dignified living standards.
- Describes a labour relations model promoting continuous dialogue with trade unions, supported by bilateral company/union bodies on equal opportunities, welfare, safety, and sustainable development.
- Assigns operational responsibility for engagement with worker representatives to the Relations with Workers’ Representative and Welfare unit under the Chief People & Culture Officer.
- Outlines structured social dialogue via the Labour Relations Protocol and multiple committees: weekly meetings with unions/Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee; Consultation Committee as needed; Joint Business Policy and Corporate Climate Committee quarterly; additional local quarterly meetings.
- Reports more than 30 agreements reached with trade unions in 2024.
- Details remediation and reporting mechanisms: Code of Ethics inbox and a 24/7 whistleblowing channel ensuring confidentiality and protection from retaliation, with references to ESRS G1 for further policy context.
- Explains that collective bargaining frameworks include procedures for assessing infringements; legal processes are followed for violations of law; the Labour Relations Protocol provides bodies (e.g., Consultation Committee) to interpret agreements and resolve local disputes.

nodes.title: Processes for engaging with own workers and their representatives
nodes.heading: 4.1.6 Processes for engaging with own workers and their representatives
nodes.start_phrase: The labour relations model, adopted and developed by the Group together with trade unions, has always promoted dialogue between the parties on a continuous basis.
nodes.summary:
- Focuses on employee representation, collective bargaining, wages, and worker engagement within the Group’s sustainability reporting.
- Coverage: Italy is the only country with a significant workforce; 100% of Italian employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, and 76% have workplace representation (social dialogue). No European Works Council, SE or SCE Works Council is in place.
- Adequate wages: All employees are paid at least an adequate minimum wage, defined by national law or collective agreements; for EEA countries, aligned with Directive (EU) 2022/2041; outside the EEA, aligned with applicable standards or collective agreements ensuring dignified living standards.
- Engagement model: A structured labour relations framework with ongoing dialogue via bilateral company/union bodies on equal opportunities, welfare, safety, and sustainability. Responsibility sits with the Relations with Workers’ Representative and Welfare unit under the Chief People & Culture Officer.
- Governance and meetings: Relations guided by an industry framework and a Labour Relations Protocol. Regular interactions include weekly meetings at Group level (e.g., Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee), ad hoc Consultation Committee meetings, quarterly Joint Business Policy and Corporate Climate Committee sessions, and quarterly local meetings. Over 30 agreements were concluded in 2024.
- Grievance and remediation: Multiple reporting channels—Code of Ethics inbox (confidential, anti-retaliation) and a 24/7 whistleblowing channel for employees and other authorized users. Collective bargaining processes and the Labour Relations Protocol provide mechanisms and committees (e.g., Consultation Committee) for assessing infringements and resolving disputes; legal proceedings are used when breaches of law occur.

nodes.title: Remediation processes for employees and their representatives and reporting channels
nodes.heading: 4.1.7 Remediation processes for employees and their representatives and reporting channels
nodes.start_phrase: The Group provides various company channels for reporting grievances, needs and concerns, such as the Code of Ethics inbox and the whistleblowing channel.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and context: Excerpt from the Consolidated Sustainability Statement focused on labor relations, worker representation, wages, grievance mechanisms, job protection targets, and reskilling actions, primarily in Italy (the only country where the Group’s workforce is significant).

- Collective bargaining and worker representation:
  - In Italy, 100% of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements.
  - Workplace representation (social dialogue) covers 76% of employees in Italy.
  - No European Works Council (EWC), SE Works Council, or SCE Works Council is in place.

- Adequate wages:
  - The Group guarantees an adequate minimum wage for all employees in every country of operation.
  - “Adequate minimum wage” is defined per national law or collective agreements; in the EEA aligned with Directive (EU) 2022/2041; outside the EEA aligned with relevant standards ensuring dignified living.

- Engagement with workers and their representatives:
  - A longstanding labor relations model fosters continuous, structured dialogue with trade unions, including bilateral company/union bodies addressing equal opportunities, welfare, safety, and sustainability.
  - Responsibility sits with the Relations with Workers’ Representative and Welfare unit under the Chief People & Culture Officer.
  - Regular meeting architecture:
    - Weekly: Group Delegation and/or Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee.
    - As needed: Consultation Committee for disputes and general labor matters.
    - Quarterly: Joint Business Policy and Corporate Climate Committee.
    - Local-level meetings generally quarterly.
  - Over 30 trade union agreements concluded in 2024.

- Grievance and remediation mechanisms:
  - Reporting channels include a confidential Code of Ethics inbox and a 24/7 whistleblowing platform for employees and third parties.
  - Collective bargaining processes provide mechanisms to assess infringements; legal escalation occurs where laws are breached.
  - The Labour Relations Protocol defines bodies and processes for interpretation and application checks; the Consultation Committee manages local disputes.
  - The Joint Business Policy and Corporate Climate Committee applies uniform criteria for assessing conduct reports and proposes preventive actions, ensuring data protection and continuous monitoring.
  - Agreements foresee specific check-ins during organizational changes.

- Job protection targets and metrics (2022–2025 Business Plan):
  - Target: 8,000 people reskilled/upskilled by 2025.
  - Achieved by 31/12/2024: 6,902 people.
  - Programs aim to redirect skills toward strategic, high value-added areas.

- Actions on job protection and labor relations:
  - Agreement of 23 October 2024 supports digital transformation and AI adoption, simplifying service models and freeing time for development, coupled with a major upskilling/reskilling plan.
  - Workforce adjustments:
    - Up to 4,000 voluntary exits by end-2027 (retirement or industry solidarity fund).
    - 4,600 new permanent hires by 31/12/2025 and an additional 3,500 by 30/06/2028 to balance exits and support growth.
    - In 2024, about 1,550 exits were matched by a similar number of hires.
  - Mixed contracts for new hires: dual arrangements combining part-time employment with self-employed financial advisor roles; 1,200 people on such contracts at end-2024.
  - 2024 reskilling focus areas: business development (Digital Branch), control functions (ENIF/KYC), technology (Application Digitalisation, Data & Analytics), and data/AI/technology (MATRIX project).
  - Nationwide deployment supported by delocalized models and the “Next Way of Working.”
  - The Group Internal Mobility & Reskilling Center manages matching of skills to needs and staffing of new areas.
  - Quarterly monitoring since 2022 and anonymous surveys indicate high satisfaction, motivation, and engagement among participants.

nodes.title: Job protection targets and metrics
nodes.heading: 4.1.5.5 Job protection targets and metrics
nodes.start_phrase: In line with 2022 –2025 Business Plan targets, Intesa Sanpaolo aims to reallocate and reskill/upskill its people capacity towards new priority initiatives, focusing on the most strategic professional roles and skills for the Group.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on job protection, labor relations, and workforce transformation within Intesa Sanpaolo’s 2022–2025 Business Plan, as part of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.
- Governance and oversight: the Joint Business Policy and Corporate Climate Committee applies uniform criteria to assess reports of conduct breaches; secure reporting via a dedicated inbox; continuous monitoring and preventive action proposals. Agreements foresee discussion and implementation checks during organizational changes through the Group Delegation, Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee, and the Consultation Committee.
- Job protection target: reskill/upskill 8,000 people by 2025; 6,902 achieved as of 31.12.2024 (baseline not applicable).
- Strategic objective: reallocate capabilities to priority, high value-added roles and skills, aligning with digitalization and AI-driven transformation.
- Key 23 Oct 2024 agreement: streamlines service/business models, frees time for professional development, and launches a major upskilling/reskilling plan to spread digital skills and cover new roles.
- Workforce planning: up to 4,000 voluntary exits by end-2027 (retirement/solidarity fund), balanced by 4,600 permanent hires by 31.12.2025 and an additional 3,500 by 30.06.2028 to support growth.
- 2024 execution: ~1,550 exits and a similar number of hires; introduction of mixed contracts combining part-time employment with self-employed financial advisor roles for out-of-branch activities; 1,200 in service on such contracts at year-end.
- Reskilling/upskilling in 2024: over 3,000 people (approx. 6,900 since 2022) trained for business development (Digital Branch), control functions (ENIF/KYC), technology projects (Application Digitalisation, Data & Analytics), and data/AI/technology training (MATRIX).
- Nationwide implementation leveraging “delocalisation” and new working methods under the “Next Way of Working” initiative.
- Operational enablers and monitoring: the Group Internal Mobility & Reskilling Center manages internal mobility and staffing; quarterly reporting since 2022; anonymous surveys of participants indicate high satisfaction, motivation, and engagement.

nodes.title: Actions related to job protection and labour relations
nodes.heading: 4.1.5.6 Actions related to job protection and labour relations
nodes.start_phrase: For Intesa Sanpaolo Group, job protection is a key element of the 2022 –2025 Business Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Governance of conduct reporting: A Joint Business Policy and Corporate Climate Committee applies uniform criteria to assess reports of behavior breaching Group values/collective agreements, using a protected inbox, with ongoing monitoring and proposals to prevent critical situations. Agreements provide structured dialogue and implementation checks during organizational changes with relevant committees.
- Job protection strategy and metrics: In line with the 2022–2025 Business Plan, the Group targets 8,000 people reskilled/upskilled by 2025; 6,902 achieved as of 31.12.2024. Programs support redeployment to strategic, higher value-added roles.
- Workforce transformation agreement (23 Oct 2024): Supports simpler customer models, frees time for professional development, and launches a major digital upskilling/reskilling push. Plans 4,000 voluntary exits by end-2027 and 4,600 permanent hires by 31.12.2025 plus 3,500 by 30.06.2028 to balance effects and sustain growth. In 2024 ~1,550 exits matched by similar hires. Introduction of mixed contracts (part-time employment plus self-employed financial advisor) with 1,200 in service at end-2024.
- Reskilling focus areas: Business development (e.g., Digital Branch), control functions (ENIF/KYC), technology (Application Digitalisation, Data & Analytics), and data/AI/technology training (MATRIX). Programs are nationwide, leveraging delocalisation and “Next Way of Working.”
- Internal mobility and monitoring: The Group Internal Mobility & Reskilling Center manages tools/processes to match skills with needs and staff new areas. Quarterly monitoring since 2022 and anonymous surveys show high satisfaction, motivation, and engagement.
- Diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I): Updated DE&I Principles guide an inclusive culture across all diversity dimensions; emphasize meritocracy, equal opportunity, zero tolerance for discrimination, and a reporting channel. Gender equity commitments include balanced hiring, balanced candidate pools for first-time managerial and senior roles, and at least one less-represented gender candidate for top management roles.
- Inclusion actions: Accessibility of premises/communication/training, equal benefits for same-sex and mixed-sex relationships, awareness and inclusive language, respect-based workplace, anti-discrimination/harassment measures, and community inclusion. Principles apply to all employees, governing bodies, and contractors; the Group promotes DE&I with Business & Corporate customers and engages stakeholders/ERGs for joint initiatives.
- 2024 DE&I updates and governance: Added Board reporting on pay gap and analysis of gender coverage in merit initiatives. The Chief People & Culture Officer sets objectives/strategy, ensures Group alignment, and reports annually to the Board and Risks and Sustainability Committee.
- Combating sexual harassment: Dedicated rules ensure prevention, zero tolerance, confidential reporting, and rigorous case management led by the DE&I head. Applies to employees, agents/advisors, temps, interns, and business partners, including work-related contexts outside the workplace (events, travel, training, off-hours).

nodes.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion
nodes.heading: 4.1.8 Diversity, equity and inclusion
nodes.start_phrase: The Group has adopted Principles on Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (“DE&I Principles”) to give concrete force to its commitment to promoting and spreading, both internally and externally, an inclusive policy that values all forms of diversity.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Intesa Sanpaolo Group’s DE&I Principles as the framework for an inclusive, merit-based, and discrimination-free workplace, with explicit zero tolerance for discrimination and dedicated reporting channels, monitored by a DE&I Control Room.
- Defines broad protection across multiple diversity dimensions (e.g., gender, identity/expression, orientation, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, socioeconomic status, nationality, culture, language, opinion).
- Articulates business and ethical rationales for DE&I (innovation, better decisions, brand reputation, talent attraction/retention, stakeholder value) informed by benchmarks and certifying bodies.
- Commits to gender equity via measurable principles: balanced annual hires; balanced candidate pools for first-time managerial and senior management roles; at least one less-represented-gender candidate in top-management pools.
- Details affirmative actions: accessibility of premises/communications/training and tools; equal benefits for same- and mixed-sex relationships; inclusive language and awareness training; fostering inclusive culture; combating discrimination/harassment; promoting inclusion in local communities.
- Specifies scope: applies to all employees and corporate bodies; contractors (agents, freelance advisors, suppliers, subcontractors) acknowledge the policy; encourages Business & Corporate customers to adopt DE&I within ESG policies.
- Strengthens stakeholder engagement, including ERGs, to co-design improvements and joint initiatives.
- Notes 2024 updates approved by the Board: added pay-gap reporting to the Board and analysis of gender coverage in merit-based initiatives; the Chief People & Culture Officer sets objectives/strategy and reports annually to the Board and the Risks & Sustainability Committee.
- Outlines “Rules for Combating Sexual Harassment”: strict zero tolerance; confidential, rigorous reporting and case management; applies to employees, agents, freelance advisors/contractors, temp staff, interns, and business partners; covers workplace, travel, training, social/business events, and relevant off-hours contexts; managed by the head of the DE&I unit.

nodes.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion policies
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.1 Diversity, equity and inclusion policies
nodes.start_phrase: The Group has adopted Principles on Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (“DE&I Principles”) to give concrete force to its commitment to promoting and spreading, both internally and externally, an inclusive policy that values all forms of diversity.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) within Intesa Sanpaolo Group, as part of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.
- Policy framework: Group-wide DE&I Principles define an inclusive culture based on respect, meritocracy, equal opportunity, and zero tolerance for discrimination. They set expected conduct, concrete commitments (including gender equity), reporting channels for breaches, and regular monitoring by the DE&I Control Room.
- Scope of diversity: Protection and inclusion across gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital/family status, age, ethnicity, religion, political/trade union affiliation, socio-economic status, nationality, language, culture, disability (physical/mental), and other personal traits, including opinion.
- Business rationale: DE&I seen as ethical duty and strategic lever for innovation, decision-making quality, brand reputation, talent attraction/retention, and stakeholder value; alignment with benchmarks and certifying bodies to identify best practices.
- Gender equity commitments: 
  - Gender balance in annual hires.
  - Gender balance in candidate pools for first managerial appointments and senior roles.
  - At least one candidate from the less-represented gender in top-management candidate pools.
- Inclusion actions: Accessibility of premises/communication/training (incl. assistive tools); equal benefits for same- and mixed-sex relationships; training and inclusive language; culture of trust and respect; combating discrimination/harassment; promoting inclusion in local communities.
- Applicability: Applies to all employees and corporate bodies. Contractors (agents, freelance advisors, suppliers, subcontractors) acknowledge a specific policy statement. The Group encourages Business & Corporate customers to adopt DE&I within their ESG policies.
- Stakeholder engagement: Active dialogue with stakeholder groups (e.g., ERGs) and co-planned initiatives.
- 2024 updates: Board-approved revision adds Board reporting on pay gap and analysis of gender coverage in merit-based initiatives.
- Governance and oversight: Chief People & Culture Officer sets objectives/strategy, ensures alignment across units, and reports annually to the Board and the Risks and Sustainability Committee.
- Anti-harassment rules: “Rules for Combating Sexual Harassment” establish zero tolerance, confidential and rigorous reporting/management led by the DE&I head, and apply to employees, agents, freelance advisors, temp staff, interns, and business partners—covering work-related contexts inside/outside the workplace. All Group companies must adopt the rules; where stricter than local law, Group rules prevail.
- Disability and chronic disease: Italy-based inter-functional working group (from Aug 2018 inclusion agreement; aligned with 2020 DE&I Principles) collaborates with trade unions via the Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee; coordinated by the Workers’ Benefits office with ~80 participants. Aims to support all people, enhance well-being, and expand welfare options.
- Workforce metrics (31 Dec 2024):
  - Age distribution: under 30: 6,339 (6.8%); 30–50: 45,024 (48.1%); over 50: 42,176 (45.1%).
  - Top management gender (26 roles defined as CEO and direct reports, Chief Audit Officer, certain deputy heads, and financial reporting manager): 20 men (76.9%), 6 women (23.1%).
- Targets and progress: The 2022–2025 Business Plan requires ~50/50 gender balance in new senior appointments to reach ~30% women in senior leadership by 2025. As of 31 Dec 2024, senior positions are 71.7% men and 28.3% women.

nodes.title: Metrics on diversity by gender and age
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.2 Metrics on diversity by gender and age
nodes.start_phrase: The table below shows the age distribution of the own workforce by number and percentage of total Group employees at 31 December 2024.
nodes.summary:
- Group-wide DE&I governance and rules: All Group banks/companies must adopt DE&I rules, adapting them with approval from the Parent Company’s DE&I unit; rules apply even when stricter than local law. Reference documents (DE&I Principles and Rules for Combating Sexual Harassment) are published on the Group website.
- Disability and chronic disease inclusion: An inter-functional working group in Italy (from the Aug 2018 inclusion agreement, aligned with Oct 2020 DE&I Principles) works with the DE&I unit and meets trade unions via the Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee. Coordinated by the Workers’ Benefits office, it involves about 80 people across functions to support inclusion, wellbeing, and expanded welfare options.
- Workforce diversity metrics (31 Dec 2024):
  - Age distribution: 6.8% under 30; 48.1% between 30–50; 45.1% over 50.
  - Top management gender: 26 executives total; 23.1% women (6), 76.9% men (20). Top management defined to include the CEO and direct reports, Chief Audit Officer, certain Deputy Heads, and the manager responsible for financial reporting.
  - Senior leadership pipeline: The 2022–2025 Business Plan targets gender-balanced new senior appointments to reach ~30% women in senior leadership by 2025; as of 2024, senior positions (first- and second-level reports to the CEO) are 28.3% women and 71.7% men.
- Equal pay policies and governance: Gender-neutral, merit-based remuneration and incentives; roles evaluated via an IPE-based Global Banding system for managers and career titles for professionals; market benchmarks by band/category/region; objective, performance-linked incentives. The Board (with the Remuneration Committee) annually reviews gender neutrality and measures the gender pay gap by country and staff category, documents causes, and initiates corrective actions. Remuneration policies are subject to an annual binding shareholder vote.
- Equal pay and pay ratio metrics (2024): Gender pay gap of 25.8% (average gross hourly pay difference female vs. male, including all cash/benefit components and accrued long-term incentives; no adjustments for role/seniority or cost-of-living; excludes Risanamento S.p.A. and Banca Intesa Russia; currencies converted at average annual rates). CEO-to-median employee total remuneration ratio: 135.2.
- Workforce engagement on DE&I: Led by the DE&I head through trade unions, employee resource/affinity groups, and surveys/listening initiatives. Biennial surveys complement climate analyses; in 2024, a survey addressed stereotypes, harassment, and gender violence, with additional one-off listening initiatives.

nodes.title: Equal pay policies
nodes.heading: 4.1.9 Equal pay policies
nodes.start_phrase: Intesa Sanpaolo Group adopts gender -neutral remuneration and incentive policies, which contribute in the pursuit of equality for all employees.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines Intesa Sanpaolo Group’s gender-neutral remuneration and incentive policies ensuring equal pay for work of equal value, with neutrality across all diversity dimensions and decisions based on merit, professional skills, and equity.
- Describes systems to apply and monitor neutrality: organizational position measurement (Global Banding System for management using IPE; professional cluster segmented by career titles and/or professional groups per collective agreements), market benchmarks by band/category/geography, and objective, performance-based incentives.
- Governance and oversight: the Board of Directors, supported by the Remuneration Committee, annually assesses policy gender-neutrality and measures the gender pay gap by country and employee segments (Risk Takers excluding BoD, BoD management and supervisory functions, and all other personnel), documenting causes and implementing corrective actions as needed.
- Policies are submitted annually to a binding shareholder vote; further details available in the Report on Remuneration Policy and Compensation Paid.
- Equal pay metric (ESRS-aligned): 2024 gender pay gap is 25.8%, calculated on average gross hourly pay including all fixed, supplementary, and variable components (LTIs on an accrual basis), without adjusting for duties, role, or seniority; scope covers all in-scope Group employees as of 31 Dec 2024, excluding Risanamento S.p.A. and Banca Intesa Russia; figures converted to euro at average annual exchange rates.
- Total remuneration ratio for 2024 is 135.2 (highest-paid individual—Group CEO—vs median employee), computed on the same scope and basis as the pay gap metric.
- No cost-of-living adjustments applied to either metric.
- Worker engagement on DE&I led by the Head of Diversity, Equity & Inclusion through trade union representatives, employee resource/affinity groups, and individual surveys/listening initiatives; surveys run biennially (e.g., 2024 questionnaire on stereotypes, harassment, and gender violence), complemented by ad hoc listening activities.

nodes.title: Metrics on equal pay
nodes.heading: 4.1.9.1 Metrics on equal pay
nodes.start_phrase: The value stated below shows the gender pay gap between male and female employees, expressed as the percentage gap in average pay levels between female and male employees, as required by the ESRS standards applied for the purposes of this Statement.
nodes.summary:
- The Intesa Sanpaolo Group applies gender-neutral remuneration and incentive policies to ensure equal pay for work of equal value, with neutrality across all diversity dimensions and decisions based on merit, skills, and equity.
- To operationalize neutrality, the Group uses: (i) organizational position measurement; (ii) a Global Banding System for management based on IPE; (iii) career titles/professional group segmentation for non-management aligned with collective agreements; (iv) market benchmarks by band, professional category, and geography; and (v) objective, performance-based incentive systems.
- Governance and oversight: the Board of Directors, supported by the Remuneration Committee, annually assesses policy gender-neutrality and measures the gender pay gap across categories (Risk Takers excluding Directors, Board—management function, Board—supervisory function, and all other personnel), documents reasons for gaps, and implements corrective actions as needed. Remuneration policies are subject to an annual binding shareholder vote; further details are in the Group’s Report on Remuneration Policy and Compensation Paid.
- Equal pay metrics (ESRS-compliant): 2024 gender pay gap is 25.8%, calculated on average gross hourly pay including all supplementary and variable components (with long-term incentives on an accrual basis), without adjustments for role, duties, or seniority. Scope covers all employees in the Consolidated Sustainability Statement perimeter as of 31 Dec 2024, excluding Risanamento S.p.A. and Banca Intesa Russia; amounts in other currencies converted at the year’s average exchange rates; no cost-of-living adjustments applied.
- Pay ratio: 2024 total remuneration rate is 135.2 (ratio of the highest-paid individual—Group CEO—to the median employee’s total remuneration), calculated on the same basis and scope as the gender pay gap; no cost-of-living adjustments applied.
- Workforce engagement on DE&I is led by the Head of Diversity, Equity & Inclusion, involving trade union representatives, employee resource/affinity groups, and individual surveys/listening initiatives. Surveys occur biennially via Climate Analysis with ad hoc DE&I modules; in 2024 a questionnaire addressed stereotypes, harassment, and gender violence, alongside additional one-off listening initiatives.

nodes.title: Processes for engaging with own workers and their representatives
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.3 Processes for engaging with own workers and their representatives
nodes.start_phrase: The engagement process with the own workforce is carried on under the responsibility of the head of Diversity, Equity & Inclusion.
nodes.summary:
- The Group enforces gender-neutral remuneration and incentive policies, guaranteeing equal pay for work of equal value and neutrality across all diversity dimensions (e.g., gender, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity, disability).
- Structures to ensure neutrality include: role evaluation systems (Global Banding for management using IPE; career titles and professional groups for other roles), market benchmarks per band/professional category/geography, and objective, performance-based incentives.
- The Board of Directors, supported by the Remuneration Committee, annually reviews policy gender-neutrality and measures the gender pay gap across defined categories (Risk Takers, Board—management and supervisory roles, and all other staff), documenting causes and implementing corrective actions when needed.
- Remuneration and incentive policies are submitted annually to a binding shareholder vote; further detail is provided in the Group’s Remuneration Policy and Compensation Report.
- Equal pay metrics: 2024 gender pay gap is 25.8%, calculated on average gross hourly pay including all cash/benefit components and long-term incentives on an accrual basis, without adjusting for role/seniority; covers all consolidated employees except Risanamento S.p.A. and Banca Intesa Russia; amounts converted at average annual FX rates; no cost-of-living adjustments.
- Pay ratio: total remuneration rate in 2024 is 135.2 (CEO’s total pay vs median employee), calculated on the same scope and basis as the pay gap; no cost-of-living adjustments.
- Workforce engagement is led by the Head of DE&I via trade unions, ERGs, and individual surveys/listening. Biennial Climate Analysis add-ons and ad hoc surveys are used; in 2024 a survey on stereotypes, harassment, and gender violence was run. Feedback informs future initiatives; unions and ERGs are engaged before and after initiatives as relevant.
- DE&I is embedded in collective bargaining (Inclusion & Equal Opportunity Protocol since 2014), with policies extending benefits to same-sex unions and initiatives on disability, including autism employability projects co-funded by the Arrotonda Solidale “round-down” program (with company top-up).
- ERGs include ISPROUD (LGBTQ+ & Allies) and ARTICOLO19 (Disability & Citizenship); inclusion content and services are promoted through internal and external channels (e.g., intranet).
- Remediation and reporting channels: Code of Ethics inbox, Whistleblowing system, and a DE&I inbox; specific Rules for Combating Sexual Harassment with a dedicated email channel. The DE&I unit convenes cross-functional working tables (DE&I, HR, Audit, Legal/Governance, Health & Safety) to ensure confidential, appropriate handling, victim support, and corrective/disciplinary actions. Psychological and legal support is available, including for incidents outside the workplace.
- Sexual-harassment reporting effectiveness is supported by mandatory annual training, monitored inboxes, one-working-day acknowledgment, and a register tracking activations and investigation outcomes.

nodes.title: Remediation processes for employees and their representatives and reporting channels
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.4 Remediation processes for employees and their representatives and reporting channels
nodes.start_phrase: Two types of channels (the Code of Ethics inbox and the Whistleblowing system) are available to Group people to report needs/concerns/alleged breaches of their rights, facilitating the Group in remedying the negative impacts they may suffer.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DE&I) governance, engagement, targets, and initiatives within the Group’s sustainability framework.
- Workforce engagement mechanisms: targeted and post-event surveys, ERG community consultations, a DE&I inbox for feedback, and advance/after-action dialogue with trade union representatives (no fixed frequency).
- Collective bargaining and policy framework: a 2014 Inclusion & Equal Opportunity Protocol embedded in enterprise-level agreements; extension of benefits to same-sex unions; inter-functional working group on disability and illness; projects to promote employability of people with autism, partly funded by the voluntary “Arrotonda Solidale” initiative.
- Employee remediation and reporting: multiple channels (Code of Ethics inbox, Whistleblowing, DE&I inbox) plus a dedicated sexual-harassment reporting system governed by specific rules; guaranteed confidentiality, anti-retaliation protections, and prompt acknowledgment; “working tables” convened by DE&I with HR, Audit, Legal/Governance, and Health & Safety to manage cases; disciplinary processes and victim support (psychological and legal), including for incidents outside work; annual mandatory training and ongoing monitoring/record-keeping.
- Disability management: dedicated HR function and inbox; regular discussion with unions; activities include IT accessibility governance, training for HR/managers/top management, and company-wide awareness initiatives.
- Measurement and feedback: anonymous aggregation of engagement outcomes to steer future actions; monitoring of reporting-channel effectiveness; a 2024 survey assessing trust in sexual-harassment reporting.
- DE&I governance: DE&I unit under the Chief People & Culture Officer; a DE&I Working Group spanning divisions and key functions; the DE&I Control Room (renamed DE&I Table) monitors adherence to DE&I Principles, especially gender equity.
- Gender-balance target: Business Plan 2022–2025 requires approx. 50/50 gender split in new senior management appointments (first- and second-level reports to the CEO); clear rules on what counts as an appointment; 2022–2024 results achieved 50% women (25) and 50% men (25).
- Inclusion culture and communication: internal/external channels promote DE&I; ERG communities (e.g., ISPROUD for LGBTQ+ and Allies, ARTICOLO19 for disability and citizenship) provide ideas and advocacy; “Words of Respect” project advances inclusive language; first “Inclusion Week” delivered multi-day awareness events for all employees.

nodes.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion targets
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.5 Diversity, equity and inclusion targets
nodes.start_phrase: The 2022 –2025 Business Plan requires a gender balance (approx. 50% male and 50% female) in new appointments to senior management positions (first and second -level reports to the CEO).
nodes.summary:
- Company rules on conduct and reporting are published on the intranet; all staff must acknowledge them and can seek guidance on interpretation. A 2024 survey examined sexual harassment reporting, including trust in reporting channels, and reaffirmed protections and anti-retaliation measures for victims and reporters, including for DE&I-related breaches.
- Disability support is managed by dedicated HR structures, with a specific inbox and intranet section; disability topics are regularly discussed with trade unions within the Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee.
- An inter-functional working group manages individual reports and broader initiatives such as IT accessibility governance, dedicated training for HR, managers of people with sensory disabilities, and top management, plus Group-wide awareness actions.
- DE&I target under the 2022–2025 Business Plan: achieve approximately 50/50 gender balance in new appointments to senior management (first- and second-level reports to the CEO), monitored quarterly by the DE&I Control Room; target setting/monitoring does not involve workforce or union engagement. Clear rules define which appointments count (promotions/access to higher levels; multiple appointments counted; horizontal or temporary step changes excluded; only formal org chart levels considered).
- Progress 2022–2024: 50 appointments female and 50 male (50/50 split).
- DE&I actions in 2024 spanned the entire Group and selected external audiences (e.g., students), including one-off and multi-month programs. The D&I unit (reporting to the Chief People & Culture Officer) led strategy, coordination, and outcome measurement; a DE&I Working Group aligned divisions and key functions. The DE&I Control Room monitored adherence to DE&I Principles (especially gender equity) and was renamed the DE&I table with updated roles and responsibilities.
- Key initiatives: “Words of Respect” to promote inclusive communication (guidelines, training, awareness for all staff) and the first “Inclusion Week” in May with five themed days and ten online events featuring internal and external speakers.

nodes.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion actions
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.6 Diversity, equity and inclusion actions
nodes.start_phrase: DE&I actions and initiatives cover all Group people, with each initiative targeted at specific clusters.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines Intesa Sanpaolo’s DE&I governance, policies and reporting channels, including mandatory acknowledgment of rules, 2024 survey on sexual harassment reporting (with a focus on trust in channels), and explicit anti-retaliation protections for reporters and victims.
- Details disability inclusion structures: a dedicated HR disability management function, a specific inbox and intranet section, and ongoing dialogue with unions through the Welfare, Safety and Sustainable Development Committee. An inter-functional working group manages individual cases and broader initiatives (IT accessibility governance, training for HR and managers of people with sensory disabilities, top management engagement, and companywide awareness).
- Sets and monitors gender-balance targets for senior appointments under the 2022–2025 Business Plan: 50% women and 50% men in new first- and second-level roles reporting to the CEO. Clarifies what counts as an “appointment” (excludes horizontal moves and temporary step-downs) and notes no workforce/union engagement in setting/monitoring. Results 2022–2024: 25 female and 25 male appointments (50/50).
- Describes DE&I organizational model: the D&I unit reports to the Chief People & Culture Officer; a DE&I Working Group ensures alignment across divisions; the DE&I Control Room was renamed the Diversity, Equity & Inclusion table with updated roles and responsibilities.
- Highlights culture and inclusion programs: “Words of Respect” for inclusive communication (guidelines, awareness, training); the first “Inclusion Week” with themed online events; continued initiatives to develop female talent (empowerment, rotations, shadowing, training); group coaching for first-time women managers; “The Art of Leadership | Mastering the Future” to build adaptive leadership (targeting managers and 750 professionals).
- Describes people-support initiatives: a program for long-term absentees to maintain connection and support return (>500 participants); parenting support for both mothers and fathers, including campaigns to challenge gender stereotypes around caregiving.
- Covers LGBTQ+ inclusion: partnership with Parks – Liberi e Uguali; workplace support for gender affirmation; growth of the ISPROUD ERG to 1,742 members, collaborating on content, events, and projects.
- Expands on training: inclusion and intercultural communication content; inclusive leadership training for all managers in Italy and extended abroad, with modules on disability and mental health (>6,500 participants); pilots and dialogue within the International Banks Division to harmonize DE&I, including the “women4Future” initiative under the People First program; intergenerational dialogue initiatives to improve cross-age collaboration.
- Notes recognitions and certifications: top-ranking banking group globally on the FTSE Diversity and Inclusion Index (7th overall); GEEIS-Diversity certification; national gender equality certification under Italy’s NRRP, with a 2024 follow-up audit assessing the gender equality management system in Italian entities.
- Summarizes actions for disability inclusion: a structured process for reasonable accommodations to ensure equal rights, projects across accessibility, communication, culture, training, and co-created initiatives; advanced “Disability Managers and the Working World” training completed by the inter-functional group and union representatives to establish a common language and approach.

nodes.title: Actions for the inclusion of people with disabilities
nodes.heading: 4.1.8.7 Actions for the inclusion of people with disabilities
nodes.start_phrase: The inter -functional working group handles and assesses with maximum care individual requests made for arrangement measures.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: programs to develop female professionals and managers; launch of “The Art of Leadership | Mastering the Future” for management and 750 professionals; group coaching for first-time women leaders; support for long-term absentees to aid return-to-work; parenting support for both mothers and fathers with campaigns to challenge gender stereotypes.
- LGBTQ+ inclusion: continued partnership with Parks – Liberi e Uguali; workplace support for gender affirmation; growth of ISPROUD ERG to 1,742 members, collaborating on content, events, and projects.
- External recognition and certifications: top-ranked global bank on the FTSE Diversity & Inclusion Index (7th overall worldwide); GEEIS-Diversity certification; gender equality certification under Italy’s NRRP with a second follow-up audit in 2024.
- Inclusion training and leadership development: intercultural communication initiatives; expanded inclusive leadership training for managers (over 6,500 people) including disability and mental health; pilot programs and DE&I dialogue across the International Banks Division; continuation of “women4Future” within “People First”; training to foster intergenerational collaboration.
- Disability inclusion actions: inter-functional working group managing individual accommodations and projects on accessibility, communication, culture, and training; advanced “Disability Managers and the Working World” course with union representatives; ARTICOLO 19 affinity group on disability; Intesa Sanpaolo Foundation’s mutual society to support employees’ disabled children; participation in external forums (e.g., “Abilitiamo la Disabilità”); initiatives like “Visite d’altri sensi” museum sensory tours and “Oltre le barriere” urban mobility accessibility project (#RealizzAbile finalist); dyslexia-friendly company status with webinars and resources; coordinated disability inclusion efforts across international banks.
- Training and development policy framework: strong emphasis on continuous upskilling aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan; reinforced governance of mandatory training in line with Supervisory Authorities’ expectations; Group-wide internal regulations requiring participation and platform-based tracking/notifications; accessibility accommodations for learners with specific needs; an annually defined Parent Company training plan covering executive compliance talks, role-based cross-cutting/specialized curricula, and extensions to subsidiaries tailored to local regulations and business needs.

nodes.title: Training and development
nodes.heading: 4.1.10 Training and development
nodes.start_phrase: Training and communication are two fundamental levers for the involvement of all the Group's people in a process of continuous growth and enhancement with the aim of guaranteeing the best professional experience.
nodes.summary:
- The “ARTICOLO 19 – Disability & Citizenship” affinity group expanded in 2024, focusing on ideas and initiatives to improve the lives of people with disabilities and their families.
- A non-profit mutual society was established by the Intesa Sanpaolo Foundation to support disabled children of Group employees.
- External engagement included participation in disability-focused conferences, notably the “Abilitiamo la Disabilità” round table to share best practices and strengthen a culture of disability management.
- Two key inclusion projects:
  - “Visite d’altri sensi” with Gallerie d’Italia: visually impaired employees acted as sensory tour guides to foster empathy and new perspectives on art (around 70 participants).
  - “Oltre le barriere” with the Innovation Center: an urban mobility accessibility project, finalist in the internal “#RealizzAbile” competition, piloted with Turin City Council and startups (44 teams involved).
- Intesa Sanpaolo has been certified Dyslexia-friendly since 2018, providing webinars and intranet resources (guides, videos, infographics, self-assessment tools) to raise awareness and support families.
- The International Banks Division collaborated with the Group DE&I unit on disability inclusion, holding three in-person meetings across all banks to share experiences and plan joint initiatives.
- Training and development:
  - Training and communication are core levers for continuous growth, aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan.
  - Enhanced oversight of mandatory training to meet Supervisory Authorities’ expectations; all employees with subordinate contracts must complete required courses, with standardized Group-wide rules and potential disciplinary measures for non-compliance.
  - Access and tracking via company training platforms with periodic reminders; tailored provisions ensure accessibility (e.g., for visually impaired employees).
  - An annually defined Parent Company training plan covers:
    - Compliance talks for top leadership on strategic and innovative topics.
    - Role-based and cross-cutting programs for managers and professionals, including regulatory-specific content.
    - Group-wide initiatives extended to subsidiaries, integrated with local/sector regulations and business needs.

nodes.title: Policies relating to the training and development of Group people
nodes.heading: 4.1.10.1 Policies relating to the training and development of Group people
nodes.start_phrase: Training and communication are two fundamental levers for the involvement of all the Group's people in a process of continuous growth and enhancement with the aim of guaranteeing the best professional experience.
nodes.summary:
- Disability and inclusion: ARTICOLO 19 – Disability & Citizenship grew in 2024 as an affinity group advancing disability-related ideas and support for employees and their families. The Intesa Sanpaolo Foundation launched a non-profit mutual society to benefit disabled children of Group employees. The Group engaged externally through conferences like “Abilitiamo la Disabilità.” Initiatives included “Visite d’altri sensi” (sensory museum tours led by visually impaired employees; ~70 participants) with Gallerie d’Italia and “Oltre le barriere” (urban mobility accessibility pilot; finalist in “#RealizzAbile”; 44 teams; with Innovation Center, Turin City Council and start-ups). Intesa Sanpaolo remains a certified Dyslexia-friendly company, offering webinars and intranet resources (guides, videos, infographics, self-assessment) on SLDs. The International Banks Division collaborated with the Group DEI unit on disability-focused inclusion across three in-person meetings.

- Training and development governance: Training and communication are core levers aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan, with strengthened control over mandatory training to meet Supervisory Authorities’ expectations. All employees must complete mandatory courses per Group regulations, with standardized Group-wide application, platform-based tracking/notifications, and accessibility accommodations (e.g., for visually impaired staff).

- Annual training plan: Defined, implemented and monitored at Parent Company level with role-based provisions and extension to subsidiaries. Components include: compliance talks for senior leaders; cross-cutting and role-specific programs for managers/professionals; and locally integrated initiatives per regulations/business needs.

- Identification of training needs: Led by the Chief People & Culture Officer area with HR, based on job requirements, legal and regulatory needs (including for products/services), strategic Group topics, and Supervisory Authorities’ findings, with in-year reviews.

- Compliance and integrity focus: Training supports AML/CFT, embargoes, antitrust, fair customer conduct, tax integrity, anti-corruption (zero tolerance), transparency, and conflict-of-interest prevention.

- ESG and social training: Target to train all employees on ESG by 2025 through a basic (online) and specialist (often in-person) track across E, S, and G. Environmental courses (mandatory for those in environmental/energy management systems) are available to all. Social topics include DEI, human rights, unconscious bias, a mandatory refresher on combating sexual harassment (implementing Group Rules), and Female Empowerment to address stereotypes and unlock potential.

- Employee involvement and delivery: The Learning Business Partner function collects, analyzes and develops needs, coordinates delivery (in-person/remote), and monitors outcomes, prioritizing mandatory initiatives and leveraging funding for continuous learning, upskilling and reskilling. The plan is shared with COWESS (a joint company–union body) for study, analysis and financing opportunities in vocational training.

nodes.title: Processes for the involvement of employees and their representatives
nodes.heading: 4.1.10.2 Processes for the involvement of employees and their representatives
nodes.start_phrase: The needs and training delivery model analysis process is guaranteed by the Learning Business Partner function which interfaces with the Human Resources functions and the Group structures for the identification and analysis of training requirements.
nodes.summary:
- Annual training needs identification: Led by the Chief People & Culture Officer Governance Area with HR support, based on job requirements, legal/regulatory obligations (including for services and product marketing), priority Group topics, supervisory authority findings, and in‑year updates.
- Compliance and integrity focus: Training underpins adherence to AML/CTF, embargoes, antitrust, customer fairness, and tax integrity; reinforces anti‑corruption (zero tolerance) and conflict‑of‑interest prevention.
- ESG culture and skills: Goal to train all Group employees in ESG by 2025 via a two‑level model—basic online modules for all, and specialist, often in‑person courses by Divisions/Governance Areas. Coverage spans environmental (ecological transition, climate, nature/biodiversity; mandatory courses for those in environmental/energy management systems and open to all) and social topics (DEI, anti‑sexual harassment, human rights, unconscious bias, female empowerment, stereotype deconstruction).
- Employee involvement and delivery process: The Learning Business Partner works with HR and Group structures through phases of needs collection, analysis, implementation coordination, and monitoring. Delivery methods (in‑person/remote) defined with a dedicated supplier. Training leverages funding for continuous learning, upskilling, and reskilling.
- Social partnership and governance: Training plan shared with the bilateral COWESS committee (company–union body per Labour Relations Protocol and National CBA) for study and funding opportunities. In 2024, a Group‑wide union agreement strengthened training as a strategic pillar to boost engagement, satisfaction, employability, and growth, with personalised upskilling/reskilling on AI, data analytics, ESG, and internationalisation. Employees can directly express training needs to managers and HR.
- Objectives and metrics for people development: Growth paths to develop internal talent and attract external candidates. Establishment of “job communities”:
  - By profession (homogeneous Titles/Professions) and by interest (cross‑functional themes like AI, Art & Culture).
  - 2022–2025 target: 20,000 people in job communities by Dec 2025; achieved 36,775 as of 31 Dec 2024 (including 22,176 with homogeneous Professions and Titles), with quarterly monitoring.
- Talent Management—“Leader of the Future” programme: Group‑wide initiative comprising:
  - International Talent Programme: ~3‑year personalised paths to build cross‑cutting, international managers; includes mentorship/tutorship by Senior Managers and structure Heads.
  - Key People: Excellence track for selected middle managers to accelerate professional/managerial growth toward leadership roles in complex contexts.
  - Core aims: enhance human capital, manage internal career pipelines to reduce external hiring for critical roles, and ensure generational renewal.

nodes.title: Objectives and metrics relating to the development of the Group's people and talent management
nodes.heading: 4.1.10.3 Objectives and metrics relating to the development of the Group's people and talent management
nodes.start_phrase: The Intesa Sanpaolo Group pursues the objective of providing its employees with growth paths based on training as a driver for the development of the talents present within the Group, as well as the ability to attract people from the outside.
nodes.summary:
- 2024 agreement with trade unions to make training a core pillar, boosting engagement, satisfaction, employability and professional growth through personalised upskilling/reskilling in AI, data analytics, ESG and internationalisation, with employees able to signal needs to managers/HR.
- Clear objectives and metrics for people development: cross-disciplinary training for all, specific learning and collaboration methods, and a structured model based on “job communities.”
- Job communities established by profession (homogeneous Professions/Titles) and by interest (e.g., AI, Art & Culture); target of 20,000 people by 2025 already exceeded, with 36,775 participants as of 31.12.2024 (22,176 with homogeneous Professions/Titles); monitored quarterly and governed by the Chief People & Culture Officer area.
- Talent Management via the “Leaders of the Future” programme, comprising:
  - International Talent Programme: 3-year personalised paths with mentorship/tutorship to develop internationally minded managers/professionals.
  - Key People: excellence path for selected middle managers toward complex leadership roles.
  Objectives: enhance human capital, manage internal growth strategically, and ensure generational renewal; expected results include continuity/stability, competitiveness, and a culture of excellence and innovation. Target ~1,000 participants (2022–2025); 975 reached by 31.12.2024.
- Training governance and delivery: Chief People & Culture Officer and the People Attraction, Skills & Learning Strategy structure oversee needs analysis, design and delivery; partnership with Digit’Ed ensures high-quality, updated content. Digital is the main channel, with live (in-person/remote) options as needed; multi-platform approach (Apprendo, Myla, Scuola dei Capi, LEA for international banks).
- 2024 measures and content focus: incentive-linked corrective mechanisms for late completion of mandatory training; updated content on Legislative Decree 231, Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Corruption; a dedicated “ICT and Security Risks” plan; and a digital Code of Conduct guide.
- All initiatives align with the 2022–2025 Business Plan, with intermediate milestones consistently met or exceeded.

nodes.title: Actions relating to the training and development of Group people
nodes.heading: 4.1.10.4 Actions relating to the training and development of Group people
nodes.start_phrase: The training activities are provided thanks to the intervention of the Chief People & Culture Officer Governance Area, which is tasked with:
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines Intesa Sanpaolo’s talent development and training initiatives within its Consolidated Sustainability Statement. It details the “Leaders of the Future” programme, aimed at ensuring continuity and stability through a robust talent pipeline, enhancing competitiveness via high-level skills acquisition and retention, and reinforcing a culture of excellence, innovation, and continuous growth. The programme targets around 1,000 colleagues over 2022–2025 across Italy and abroad, encompassing both the International Talent Programme (including participants in and graduates of the pathway) and the stable Key People population. As of 31 December 2024, 975 people had been involved, approaching the 2025 target of 1,000.

The document also describes Group-wide training governance led by the Chief People & Culture Officer Governance Area, responsible for promoting an inclusive change-ready culture, defining training proposals, ensuring skills updating and regulatory compliance, and preparing the Training Plan. The People Attraction, Skills & Learning Strategy structure manages needs analysis, delivery model selection, and training rollout, supported by suppliers and relevant Group units.

Training—especially mandatory—relies primarily on digital delivery to ensure rapid, scalable, and flexible access, with live classrooms used when needed. Collaboration with Digit’Ed S.p.A., established in 2022 after transferring the training business line, continued in 2024, leveraging the Group’s learning infrastructures. Multi-channel learning was advanced through platforms such as Apprendo, Myla, Scuola dei Capi (Management School), and LEA for international subsidiary banks. Incentive-linked corrective mechanisms were maintained in 2024 to address non-completion of mandatory training.

Content-wise, training was expanded to reflect regulatory updates (Legislative Decree 231, Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Corruption), a dedicated “ICT and Security Risks” plan was launched to raise awareness amid growing digitalization and geopolitical complexity, and a digital guide on the Code of Conduct was published.

nodes.title: Training activities at Group level and across departments
nodes.heading: 4.1.10.4.1 Training activities at Group level and across departments
nodes.start_phrase: The training activities are provided thanks to the intervention of the Chief People & Culture Officer Governance Area, which is tasked with:
nodes.summary:
- Focus on the “Leaders of the Future” talent strategy: goals are continuity/stability, competitiveness, and a culture of excellence and innovation. Target of about 1,000 participants over 2022–2025; 975 involved by 31/12/2024 across the International Talent Programme (includes active and alumni) and a stable “Key People” cohort. Participants receive tailored development (top business school training in English, premium coaching, empowerment, innovation workshops, and project work). These paths feed into qualitative assessments of employee well-being impacts.
- Group training governance and delivery: led by the Chief People & Culture Officer Governance Area and the People Attraction, Skills & Learning Strategy structure. Strong partnership with Digit’Ed S.p.A.; digital-first delivery via platforms (Apprendo, Myla, Scuola dei Capi, LEA), with live classrooms when needed. Digital channels enable rapid updates, on-demand access, and self-paced learning.
- Reinforced compliance: 2024 incentive mechanisms tied to timely completion of mandatory training.
- Expanded training content: updates on Legislative Decree 231, Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Corruption; a dedicated “ICT and Security Risks” plan (phishing, cyberfraud, emerging threats); MATRIX project to build IT capabilities through onboarding, specialist tracks, and certifications.
- Risk culture: awareness initiatives on current and prospective risks, including climate and technological risks.
- ESG and ethics: training on EU Taxonomy and mandatory CSRD modules; Code of Ethics training; mandatory Modern Slavery modules addressing UK and Australian requirements; a compliance talk for senior directors on ethics, modern slavery, and sexual harassment.
- Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: continued programs on female empowerment, parenting, aging; new initiatives on interculturality, inclusive leadership, disability, and inclusive language.
- Knowledge sharing: 31 Digital Talks in 2024 on topics like circular economy and organizational well-being.
- Job communities and enablement: four new communities launched in 2024 (total 12 active: 7 by profession, 5 by interest); rollout of a dedicated communities app; professional titling model extended, including a new model for the CDAITO area and updates across divisions.
- Division-level initiatives: IMI Corporate & Investment Banking advanced intercultural/generational effectiveness, ESG awareness (including the SHAPE community) and launched the “IMI CIB Next Generation Education Program” with Digit’Ed and SDA Bocconi; the Insurance Division ran ESG briefings on risks, regulation, strategy, and promoted intercultural collaboration.

nodes.title: Initiatives at the division level
nodes.heading: 4.1.10.4.2 Initiatives at the division level
nodes.start_phrase: The IMI Corporate & Investment Banking Division has promoted initiatives aimed at recognising the role and effects of stereotypes that hinder the effectiveness of intercultural and generational relationships in order to provide tools to overcome them and create bridges for collaboration, thereby enhancing everyone's differences and contribution.
nodes.summary:
- Group-wide training and culture initiatives:
  - Cybersecurity awareness and risk culture training, including climate change and technological innovation risks.
  - MATRIX Project to build HR models/tools and invest in IT upskilling; onboarding for new hires and specialist certification paths for existing professionals.
  - ESG education covering EU Taxonomy and new mandatory CSRD modules.
  - Mandatory Code of Ethics training; Modern Slavery modules aligned with UK and Australian Acts; compliance talk for directors on ethics, modern slavery, and harassment.

- Diversity, Equity & Inclusion:
  - Ongoing programs on female empowerment, parenting, aging, interculturality, inclusive leadership, disability, and inclusive language.
  - 31 Digital Talks on themes such as circular economy and organizational well-being.

- Job communities and professional frameworks:
  - Expansion to 12 job communities (7 by profession, 5 by interest) with four new communities in 2024.
  - Launch of a dedicated mobile app for communities (June 2024).
  - Extension and updates of the professional Titling model, including the CDAITO Governance Area.

- Talent development:
  - “Leaders of the Future” program (2022–2025) offering bespoke development: top business school training in English, premium coaching, international innovation workshops, and project work; used as a qualitative indicator of employee well-being impact.

- Division-level initiatives:
  - IMI Corporate & Investment Banking: training to counter stereotypes and enhance intercultural/generational collaboration; ESG positioning updates for the SHAPE community; Next Generation Education Program with Digit’Ed and SDA Bocconi featuring ESG content.
  - Insurance Division: ESG overview on market impacts, regulation, risks/opportunities, and management insights; intercultural collaboration initiatives.
  - Asset Management (Eurizon): Higher Education course for under-35s with modules on governance, ethics/behaviors, and “The ESG wave”; intercultural collaboration activities.
  - Chief Audit Officer: ESG course with AIIA tailored to audit activities.
  - International Banks Division: sustained ESG training across subsidiaries (Code of Ethics, “ISP4ESG,” “Circular Economy Plafond,” “EU Taxonomy”); live course “ESG: Disclosing Sustainability”; manager Digital Talks on macro trends, leadership, inclusive leadership; “People First” program with webinars (Climate Change, fair trade, Patagonia), ESG Gamification Experience across multiple banks, Aworld app sustainability contest, and ongoing talks on leadership/innovation.

- Health and safety:
  - Central Health & Safety function ensures compliance (Legislative Decree 81/08) as part of Group Compliance.
  - Framework includes: Occupational Health, Safety and Welfare Policy; Group Health and Safety, Environment and Energy Management Policies and Systems; corporate OHS rules for Italy.
  - Integration with the Code of Ethics and human rights commitments; clear task/responsibility system with employer accountability.
  - Certifications: ISO 9001, ISO 45001, ISO 45003.
  - Policies available to employees via intranet and to external stakeholders via the corporate website.

nodes.title: Health and safety
nodes.heading: 4.1.11 Health and safety
nodes.start_phrase: The Health & Safety structure ensures the monitoring of compliance risk with reference to the areas of occupational health and safety protection, pursuant to Legislative Decree 81/08, fulfilling the role of specialist function provided for by the Group Compliance Guidelines.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on ESG-focused training and culture-building across the Group, especially within the Asset Management Division and International Banks Division (IBD).
- Asset Management Division: continued the “Eurizon Higher Education” program with ESG modules on governance, ethics/behaviors, and the ESG wave; promoted intercultural collaboration initiatives.
- Chief Audit Officer: developed an in-depth ESG course with Group Learning Strategy and Digit’Ed, in partnership with AIIA, tailored to auditors.
- IBD: continued Digital Talks for managers on macroeconomic trends, leadership, new ways of working, and inclusive leadership; delivered broad ESG training across all banks.
- Training portfolio included mandatory Code of Ethics e-learning and non-mandatory ESG courses such as “ISP4ESG,” “Circular Economy Plafond,” and “EU Taxonomy,” plus the live course “ESG: Disclosing Sustainability.”
- Additional ESG knowledge-sharing via English-language digital talks: “ESG: Human traces in the environmental evolution” and “Urban Re-generation” on sustainable architecture.
- “People First” program launched to raise ESG awareness: three themed webinars (Climate Change; fair trade chocolate; Patagonia case), expansion of the “ESG Gamification Experience” across multiple banks and head office, an Aworld app-based sustainability contest culminating in a Sustainability Journey, and monthly Digital Talks on leadership/innovation.
- Health and Safety governance: centralized function monitors compliance with Italy’s Legislative Decree 81/08 under Group Compliance Guidelines.
- Policy framework: Occupational Health, Safety and Welfare Policy; Group-level Health and Safety, Environment and Energy Management Policies and Systems; and corporate rules for the Italian perimeter defining roles, responsibilities, and accident prevention activities, with employer accountability.
- Alignment with the Group Code of Ethics and international human rights standards; certifications achieved include ISO 9001, ISO 45001, and ISO 45003.
- Transparency and access: policies and systems available on the Group intranet and the institutional website.

nodes.title: Health and safety policies
nodes.heading: 4.1.11.1 Health and safety policies
nodes.start_phrase: The Health & Safety structure ensures the monitoring of compliance risk with reference to the areas of occupational health and safety protection, pursuant to Legislative Decree 81/08, fulfilling the role of specialist function provided for by the Group Compliance Guidelines.
nodes.summary:
- Extensive ESG education and awareness:
  - Asset Management Division’s 2024 “Eurizon Higher Education” with ESG-focused modules; intercultural initiatives to foster collaboration and inclusion.
  - Chief Audit Officer’s specialized ESG course for auditors developed with AIIA.
  - International Banks Division (IBD) continued ESG training across subsidiary banks: mandatory Code of Ethics; optional courses (ISP4ESG, Circular Economy Plafond, EU Taxonomy); live “ESG: Disclosing Sustainability”; English digital talks on environmental evolution and urban regeneration.
  - “People First” program: Division-wide webinars (climate change, fair trade chocolate, Patagonia), ESG Gamification across multiple banks, Aworld app contest culminating in a Sustainability Journey, and ongoing Digital Talks on leadership and innovation.

- Health and safety governance framework:
  - Health & Safety structure ensures compliance with Italian Legislative Decree 81/08.
  - Group-wide policies and systems: Occupational Health, Safety and Welfare Policy; Health and Safety, Environment and Energy Management Policies and Systems; corporate rules defining tasks and responsibilities, with employer accountability.
  - Alignment with human rights commitments in the Code of Ethics; certifications ISO 9001, ISO 45001, ISO 45003; documents accessible via intranet and institutional website.

- Employee involvement and representation:
  - Dialogue supported by Code of Ethics and Labour/Management Relations Protocol.
  - 96 Worker Safety Representatives (covering 100% of Italian workforce), with 40 in periodic meetings with Safety and Protection functions; information and training via intranet and mandatory platforms.
  - Process Guides define Safety Officer roles and communication responsibilities.

- Reporting and remediation mechanisms:
  - Compliance Management Process Guide governs anomaly handling, corrective actions, and communication channels.
  - Multiple reporting avenues for risks/incidents (branch managers, WSRs), checks by head office, direct channels for Occupational Medicine; psychological support after traumatic events.
  - Systematic risk monitoring and assessment: employer-led risk assessments, inspections/audits by the Prevention and Protection Service, tracked risk factors and interventions; training on secure, privacy-protective reporting.

- Objectives and proactive actions:
  - Continuous monitoring and protection without fixed quantitative targets.
  - Initiatives beyond legal requirements addressing emerging risks: stress, subjective vulnerabilities (from 2024), neuroscientific research on cognitive load, technostress, aging; training industrialized; focus on human-computer interaction and acoustic well-being.
  - Comprehensive risk assessment through technical and field analyses, measurements, and a Risk Assessment Document (DVR); ISO 45003 certification on psychosocial risk management confirmed for the second consecutive year.

nodes.title: Processes for the involvement of employees and their representatives
nodes.heading: 4.1.11.2 Processes for the involvement of employees and their representatives
nodes.start_phrase: The Group's commitment to involving people is expressed in the Code of Ethics, promoting listening and dialogue at all levels.
nodes.summary:
- Employee involvement and union relations: Commitment to listening and dialogue per the Code of Ethics; engagement with trade unions via a Labour/Management Relations Protocol establishing a structured union relations model.
- Worker Safety Representatives (WSRs): 96 WSRs covering 100% of workers in Italy; 40 participate in periodic meetings with the Safety and Protection Department and employer delegate; health and safety information shared via intranet and mandatory training (Apprendo platform).
- Governance and roles: Process Guides define responsibilities, including the Safety Officer’s role in employee engagement and communication on safety matters.
- Remediation and reporting channels: A Compliance Management Process Guide governs handling of safety-related anomalies and corrective actions; multiple reporting channels exist (including Code of Ethics/whistleblowing), with specific access for branch managers, WSRs, and Occupational Medicine; mechanisms to open, record, assess, and track risk factors; psychological support available after traumatic events.
- Risk assessment and monitoring: Employer responsible for risk assessment; Prevention and Protection Service conducts inspections/audits and records results; systems track acceptance and completion of interventions; supervisors trained on proper use of reporting channels with privacy safeguards.
- Health and safety objectives: Ongoing monitoring and actions to protect employees, maintaining standards without fixed quantitative targets.
- Initiatives beyond compliance: Tools from Occupational Health Doctor for emerging risks (new stress forms, 2024 subjective vulnerabilities); neuroscientific projects on cognitive load, technostress, aging (with training industrialized in 2024); focus areas include Human-Computer Interaction and Acoustic Well-being alongside traditional prevention and continuous training.
- Risk evaluation methodology: Technical and field analyses of all workplaces, on-site measurements by qualified staff when needed; Risk Assessment Document (DVR) reflects implemented measures and their effectiveness; prevention/protection measures and PPE specified in Process Guides.
- Certifications: ISO 45003 certification for psychosocial risk management confirmed for the second consecutive year.

nodes.title: Remediation processes for employees and their representatives and reporting channels
nodes.heading: 4.1.11.3 Remediation processes for employees and their representatives and reporting channels
nodes.start_phrase: The management of material impacts on the Group's people in the health and safety area is governed by a specific Process Guide (Compliance Management Process Guide - Management of Occupational Safety Regulations) which sets out the approach to managing the anomalies identified through control activities and any corrective actions to be implemented.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on employee involvement and representation in health and safety, anchored in the Group’s Code of Ethics and a Labour/Management Relations Protocol that structures union relations and dialogue.
- Central role of Worker Safety Representatives (96 WSRs covering 100% of Italian workers; 40 participate in periodic meetings with the Safety and Protection Department and the employer’s delegate) to communicate with employees, gather perspectives, and review Prevention and Protection Service activities. Information is shared via the intranet and mandatory training (Apprendo).
- Process Guides define roles and responsibilities, including the Safety Officer’s duties for communication, employee engagement, and oversight of occupational safety compliance.
- Clear remediation and reporting mechanisms through a Compliance Management Process Guide: channels for employees to communicate with health and safety functions; risk/incident reporting by branch managers and WSRs with full workplace access; head office verification; direct channels for branch managers and Occupational Medicine (e.g., to request additional exams); psychological support after traumatic events.
- Structured risk monitoring and assessment: employer-led risk assessment; Prevention and Protection Service conducts inspections/audits for integrated risk assessment; risk factors are recorded, tracked for acceptance, and monitored through to intervention completion. Supervisors receive training on secure, privacy-protecting reporting channels available on the intranet.
