nodes.title: Meals
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.1.1 Meals
nodes.start_phrase: Food poverty is one of the most dramatic aspects for people in fragile and destitute conditions.
nodes.summary:
- Focus area: “Combating poverty” within the Consolidated Sustainability Statement, delivered through the Food and Shelter Programme across Italy, targeting vulnerable groups including children, the elderly, people in rehab communities, and individuals connected to the prison system.
- Meals: Broad anti–food-poverty network with key partnerships:
  - Fondazione Banco Alimentare, including “Ri-pescato” (recovery of illegal fish seized in Sicily for charitable distribution).
  - Fondazione San Patrignano (“Support and Prevent” to provide meals for community residents).
  - Fondazione Dynamo Camp (free meals and beds for children with disabilities/serious illnesses in Tuscany).
  - Vidas ODV (free daily meals for young hospice patients and families at Casa Sollievo Bimbi, Milan).
  - Semi di Vita cooperative (free distribution of harvests to charities, minors in Bari’s Fornelli Juvenile Detention Centre, and youths under alternative measures).
  - Fondazione Cometa (“A tavola per Crescere Insieme” with Il Manto day centre for children from families in difficulty).
  - Results: 43.5 million meals distributed in 2022–2024 via partnerships; Charity Allowance of €2.4m enabled ~1.4 million meals/year (~3,800/day) and additional pathways out of poverty.
- Beds: Structured shelter interventions enhancing dignity, healthcare access, and caregiver support:
  - Support to San Patrignano, Dynamo Camp, Vidas ODV to expand reception capacity for children, youths, and families.
  - Collaboration with Di.Re (Women’s Network against Violence) funding initial utilities/rent for Shelter Homes, babysitting during job search, and work-start goods.
  - Results: 3.9 million beds provided in 2022–2024.
- Medicines: National network expansion with Fondazione Banco Farmaceutico:
  - “Pharma Links” to create/strengthen drug collection and distribution networks.
  - Enhancement of the “Recupero Farmaci Validi” model (recovering unused valid medicines) and the BFOnline management platform.
  - Results: 6.1 million medicines prescribed/provided in 2022–2024.
- Clothing: Circular redistribution via “Golden Links” with Caritas Italiana and corporate clients, delivering unsold/returned/second-choice/usable defective items to families in hardship.
  - Results: ~560,000 clothing and other goods distributed in 2022–2024.
- Governance: Quarterly monitoring of programme effectiveness through partner reports.

nodes.title: Beds
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.1.2 Beds
nodes.start_phrase: The initiatives aimed at providing beds developed and implemented by Intesa Sanpaolo aim to enable a structured intervention that provides dignified shelter, but is also able to guarantee better access to healthcare and support for caregivers.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Intesa Sanpaolo’s “Food and shelter programme for people in need” within the Consolidated Sustainability Statement, targeting vulnerable groups across Italy (children, elderly, people in rehab centres, and those connected to the prison system).
- Meals: Broad anti–food-poverty network with Fondazione Banco Alimentare (including “Ri-pescato” fish recovery in Sicily), Fondazione San Patrignano (“Support and Prevent”), Fondazione Dynamo Camp, Vidas ODV (Casa Sollievo Bimbi, Milan), Semi di Vita (Bari), and Fondazione Cometa (“A tavola per Crescere Insieme”). Results: 43.5 million meals distributed in 2022–2024. Charity Allowance contributed €2.4m for ~1.4 million meals in one year (~3,800/day) and supports broader poverty-exit pathways.
- Beds: Support for dignified shelter and care access via San Patrignano, Dynamo Camp, Vidas ODV, and Di.Re (women’s “Shelter Homes,” covering initial utilities/rent, babysitting, and start-up goods). Results: 3.9 million beds provided in 2022–2024.
- Medicines: Expansion of national medicine collection/distribution with Fondazione Banco Farmaceutico through “Pharma Links,” strengthening “Recupero Farmaci Validi” and the “BFOnline” platform. Results: 6.1 million drugs prescribed in 2022–2024.
- Clothing: Circular redistribution of apparel with Caritas Italiana and corporate clients via “Golden Links,” delivering unsold/returned/second-choice usable items to families in hardship. Results: ~560,000 items distributed in 2022–2024.
- Monitoring: Quarterly performance tracking based on reports from partner organizations.

nodes.title: Medicines
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.1.3 Medicines
nodes.start_phrase: Access to healthcare is a right to which every citizen is entitled, and this also forms the basis for Intesa Sanpaolo's coord ination action with Banco Farmaceutico for the extension of a national network for the collection and distribution of medicines.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Intesa Sanpaolo’s Consolidated Sustainability Statement section on combating poverty through the “Food and Shelter Programme for People in Need” across Italy, targeting communities including children, the elderly, people in rehab centers, and individuals connected to the prison system.

- Meals: Extensive anti–food poverty actions via partnerships with:
  - Fondazione Banco Alimentare (including “Ri-pescato” recovery of seized fish in Sicily),
  - Fondazione San Patrignano (“Support and Prevent”),
  - Fondazione Dynamo Camp and Vidas ODV (support for children with disabilities/serious illnesses and their families),
  - Semi di Vita cooperative (Bari-area charities, minors in Fornelli Juvenile Detention Centre, and youths under alternative measures),
  - Fondazione Cometa (“A tavola per Crescere Insieme” with Il Manto day center).
  Outcomes: 43.5 million meals delivered in 2022–2024; Charity Allowance contributed €2.4m for ~1.4 million meals in one year (~3,800/day) and funded complementary pathways to help beneficiaries exit poverty.

- Beds: Actions to provide dignified shelter and improve healthcare access/caregiver support through collaborations with San Patrignano, Dynamo Camp, Vidas ODV, and Di.Re – Donne in Rete contro la violenza (supporting women leaving violence via Shelter Homes, initial utilities/rent, babysitting, and starter goods for work activities). Outcome: 3.9 million beds made available in 2022–2024.

- Medicines: With Fondazione Banco Farmaceutico through the “Pharma Links” project to build national drug collection/distribution networks, expand “Recupero Farmaci Validi” (unused medicines recovery), and strengthen the BFOnline management platform. Outcome: 6.1 million drugs prescribed in 2022–2024.

- Clothing: “Golden Links” with Caritas Italiana and corporate clients to recover and redistribute unsold/returned/second-choice/usable defective apparel to families in need. Outcome: ~560,000 items distributed in 2022–2024.

- Monitoring: Programme effectiveness tracked quarterly via partner reports.

nodes.title: Clothing
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.1.4 Clothing
nodes.start_phrase: The distribution of items of clothing has become an opportunity to design a complex circular redistribution initiative to con firm the combination of sustainability and social issues.
nodes.summary:
- Focus areas: Combating poverty and fostering social cohesion/inclusion across Italy within Intesa Sanpaolo’s Consolidated Sustainability Statement, with regular monitoring of outcomes.
- Food and Shelter Programme:
  - Meals: Extensive partnerships to tackle food poverty, including Fondazione Banco Alimentare (with “Ri-pescato” illegal-fish recovery in Sicily), Fondazione San Patrignano (“Support and Prevent”), Dynamo Camp and Vidas ODV for young patients/families, Semi di Vita cooperative (Bari area and juvenile justice context), and Fondazione Cometa for children in after-school care. Impact 2022-2024: 43.5 million meals; Charity Allowance: €2.4m for ~1.4m meals/year (~3,800/day), plus pathways to help beneficiaries exit poverty.
  - Beds: Support for dignified shelter and access to care via San Patrignano, Dynamo Camp, Vidas ODV, and Di.Re (women escaping violence) covering utilities/rent, caregiving, babysitting, and start-up work goods. Impact 2022-2024: 3.9 million beds provided.
  - Medicines: National drug collection/distribution with Banco Farmaceutico via “Pharma Links,” scaling “Recupero Farmaci Validi” and the BFOnline platform. Impact 2022-2024: 6.1 million drugs prescribed/donated.
  - Clothing: “Golden Links” with Caritas Italiana and corporate partners to recover and redistribute unsold/returned/second-choice apparel. Impact 2022-2024: ~560,000 items distributed.
  - Monitoring: Quarterly reporting from partner entities.
- Social cohesion and inclusion:
  - Broad support to non-profits through funding, co-planning, and know-how transfer to bolster vulnerable groups; initiatives monitored jointly with partners.
  - “Aiutare chi Aiuta” with Caritas Italiana: inclusion of elderly, youth poverty relief (meals, health kits, clothing) and, in 2024, enhanced support for incarcerated people and families through training and job placement. 31 new projects in 2024; 54 ongoing in total.
  - “QuBì – La ricetta contro la povertà”: multi-pronged child and family poverty response in Milan; support to Caritas Ambrosiana Emporiums/Solidarity Shops. 2024 reach: ~7,400 people (incl. ~2,700 minors), ~2,400 families.
  - Hospital nursery education for long-term pediatric patients (0–36 months) with Consorzio PAN cooperatives; over 785 children served to 2024.
  - Disability inclusion: “Comunità Amiche della Disabilità” to define and scale inclusive territorial models and strategic planning.
  - Energy poverty and urban regeneration: Creation of Solidarity Renewable Energy Communities in Naples (“Sharing Energy”) with low/free energy for vulnerable people; partnership with Fondazione della Comunità del Mediterraneo for energy sharing at Fondo Saccà; “La Bella Piazza” regenerating Piazza Garibaldi, Naples.
  - Youth inclusion and education: “In Action ESG NEET” training for social/healthcare and educational roles (~150 participants; 67% employed or resumed study within months); “WeBecome” primary-school programme on civic education (3,460+ schools; 4,000+ platform users incl. 2,400+ teachers).
  - Social housing: 2022–2025 plan to expand affordable homes and student residence beds in response to economic fragility and student housing needs.

nodes.title: Social cohesion and inclusion
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.2 Social cohesion and inclusion
nodes.start_phrase: The Group values its support to the communities, including through initiatives aimed at developing local territories in favou r of people in conditions of socio -economic fragility, with the aim of ensuring social cohesion and inclusion.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Intesa Sanpaolo’s community impact under its 2022–2025 Business Plan, with an emphasis on social cohesion, inclusion, youth education, employability, and social/urban redevelopment. Initiatives are co-designed with nonprofits, financially supported by the Bank, and monitored for effectiveness.

- Poverty alleviation and inclusion:
  - “Aiutare chi Aiuta” with Caritas Italiana: supports elderly and youth in poverty; in 2024 expanded to assist incarcerated individuals and families with essentials, training, and job placement; 31 new projects, 54 ongoing total.
  - “QuBì – La ricetta contro la povertà” (Fondazione Cariplo and partners): identifies families in need, facilitates access to food, and strengthens neighborhood support; backed Caritas Ambrosiana’s 3 Emporiums and 6 Solidarity Shops; ~7,400 beneficiaries in 2024 (incl. ~2,700 minors), ~2,400 families.
  - Hospital nursery program for long-term pediatric oncohematology patients (with Consorzio PAN): combats isolation and supports cognitive/emotional development; 785+ children served since launch.
  - “Comunità Amiche della Disabilità”: defines and scales inclusive territorial models for people with disabilities.

- Energy poverty and urban regeneration:
  - “Sharing Energy – Rinnoviamo l’energia” in Naples: builds Solidarity Renewable Energy Communities (CERS), distributing low-cost/free renewable energy to vulnerable households.
  - Partnership with Fondazione della Comunità del Mediterraneo Sostenibile e Solidale: pilots solidarity energy communities via the redevelopment of Fondo Saccà, using storage/sharing and social algorithms.
  - “La Bella Piazza” in Naples: public space regeneration to counter social and urban degradation.

- Youth inclusion and civic education:
  - “In Action ESG NEET”: training for roles in care, social assistance, and education; ~150 participants; 67% employed or back in study post-course.
  - “WeBecome”: primary school civic and inclusion program; 3,460+ schools involved; 4,000+ platform users, incl. 2,400+ teachers.

- Social housing and student accommodation:
  - Large-scale program to expand affordable housing and student beds; progress tracked via financial and managerial KPIs.
  - Key projects: MilanoSesto (with Coima, Redo) integrating subsidized/unrestricted housing (~27,000 sqm), City of Health and Research, and mixed-use/park; support to the Coima–Covivio–Prada consortium at former Porta Romana (Olympic Village → 1,700 subsidized beds).
  - 2024 investments in iGeneration and Pitagora funds (InvestiRe, Finint) and Redo’s Montelungo–Colleoni (Bergamo), enabling 4,800+ additional beds.

- Youth education and employability (nationwide):
  - “Giovani e Lavoro” (with Fondazione Generation Italy ETS/McKinsey): free training for 18–29 NEETs in high-demand sectors (Hi-Tech, precision mechanics, sales, hospitality); since 2019: 4,850+ trainees, 2,480+ companies, >80% placement.
  - “Digital Re-start” (with Fideuram, Talent Garden): digital reskilling for unemployed 40+; 5th edition in 2024 with 50 beneficiaries (Rome, Milan).
  - 2024 initiatives for workplace inclusion of people with disabilities; support for migrants/refugees via training and work pathways.
  - “Generation4Universities” (Generation Italy, McKinsey, Intesa): training, mentorship, and bootcamp for high-potential university students; 2024: 90 students, 50 universities, 19 partner firms.
  - “Zeta Lab” and “Offerta Modulare”: employee-tutored courses in secondary schools; ~2,400 students across 40+ schools in 2024.
  - “FUTURA” (Save the Children, ForumDD, Yolk, with Intesa): combats female educational poverty and early school leaving with personalized plans for 300 girls/young women (incl. 50 young mothers); ~320 plans activated and a structured impact evaluation framework.

nodes.title: Youth education and employability
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.3 Youth education and employability
nodes.start_phrase: Intesa Sanpaolo is also committed to supporting the community through initiatives dedicated to the training and job placement of people in situations of social or economic vulnerability.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on Intesa Sanpaolo’s social impact initiatives in Italy, emphasizing inclusion, reduction of inequalities, and measurable outcomes.
- Urban regeneration and housing: partnerships with Coima, Redo, Covivio and Prada to advance major projects such as MilanoSesto and the former Porta Romana rail yard (Olympic Village legacy), plus expanded support for student housing via investments in iGeneration and Pitagora funds and Redo’s Bergamo initiative, enabling over 4,800 new beds.
- Youth education and employability: programmes to improve access to quality education, prevent dropouts and connect training to labour-market needs, especially for vulnerable groups.
- “Giovani e Lavoro”: nationwide training for NEETs (18–29) in high-demand sectors, fully funded by the Bank; since 2019, 4,850+ trained/in training, 2,480+ companies involved, and 80%+ placement.
- “Digital Re-start”: reskilling for unemployed 40+ with Fideuram and Talent Garden; 2024’s 5th edition supported 50 beneficiaries in Rome and Milan.
- Inclusion initiatives for people with disabilities, migrants and refugees through skills development and work integration.
- “Generation4Universities”: soft-skills training, mentorship and bootcamp; in 2024 involved 90 students, 50 universities and 19 companies.
- School-based engagement: “Zeta Lab” and “Offerta Modulare” with Bank employees as tutors; ~2,400 students across 40+ schools in 2024.
- Targeted programmes against female educational poverty: “FUTURA” (Save the Children, partners and Intesa Sanpaolo) with 320+ individualized plans, and a scalable evaluation model.
- Place-based education and work inclusion: Northern Naples “Educational Ecosystem” hub supporting training, guidance and psychological services; ~250 students engaged in 2024/2025 after Bank-backed renovations.
- Capacity building for the third sector: Executive Master with 24ore Business School and 30 scholarships on digitalization and innovation.
- Health: financing the new pediatric hemodialysis department at Bambino Gesù Children’s Hospital, improving annual care for about 100 young patients.
- Crowdfunding and community support: “For Funding” platform with rigorous due diligence, zero fees for donors, and integrated communications; complemented by the “Formula” programme with CESVI selecting local NPO projects every four months; in 2024, €8.7m raised overall, €6.1m allocated to Formula, with structured reporting and impact tracking.

nodes.title: Health and healthcare
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.4 Health and healthcare
nodes.start_phrase: It is estimated that in Italy approximately 30,000 boys and girls under the age of 18 suffer from chronic kidney disease (CKD ), a disease that involves the progressive and irreversible loss of kidney function, which is unable to perform its vital functions properly.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on education and social inclusion: evaluation of interventions improving girls’ and young women’s formal and informal skills, with a goal to make successful methodologies replicable and scalable nationally.
- Launch of the “Ecosistema Educativo per i giovani e le famiglie di Napoli Nord” led by Istituto Mater Dei with the Campania Region to combat educational poverty and youth marginalization (ages 13–25) in Caivano, Casoria, and Salicelle. Creation of an educational hub offering three-year education and vocational training, orientation, and active labor policy services, plus job guidance and psychological support. The Group funded renovations, classrooms, and labs. Early impact: around 250 students enrolled in 2024/2025.
- Capacity building for the non-profit sector: an Executive Master with 24ore Business School, including 30 scholarships, to address digitalization and technology challenges and to foster local social networks and alliances.
- Health and healthcare: support for the new pediatric hemodialysis department at Bambino Gesù Children’s Hospital (5-month project completed Dec 2024), including structural upgrades and service improvements for young patients and families. Expected annual benefit: improved dialysis services for about 100 pediatric patients.
- Crowdfunding for social impact: Intesa Sanpaolo’s For Funding platform continues as a leading national tool supporting NPO projects in areas such as emergency/poverty, healthcare, social inclusion, community welfare, and environmental/cultural heritage. NPOs undergo a structured selection and due diligence process; donations are facilitated via web/app; the Bank covers 100% of operating costs; campaign durations are customizable.
- “Formula” program within For Funding: quarterly selection of 13 NPOs with Intesa Sanpaolo Regional Governance Centres and CESVI ETS, delivering targeted local projects, enhancing NPO planning/reporting capacity. In 2024, approximately €8.7 million was raised on For Funding, with about €6.1 million allocated to Formula. NPOs provide detailed progress reporting, and impact is tracked to ensure tangible community outcomes.

nodes.title: Crowdfunding platforms
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.5 Crowdfunding platforms
nodes.start_phrase: To offer a direct contribution to the implementation of social initiatives of non -profit sector organisations, the Group promotes various fundraising tools.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on education, social inclusion, and scalable methodologies to support girls and young women, aiming to replicate effective interventions nationally.
- Launch of the “Ecosistema Educativo per i giovani e le famiglie di Napoli Nord” to combat educational poverty and youth marginalization in Caivano, Casoria, and Salicelle:
  - Creation of an educational hub offering three-year education and vocational training, career guidance, active labor policies, and psychological support.
  - Group financed renovation and outfitting of classrooms and labs.
  - Approximately 250 students enrolled in new courses for the 2024/2025 school year.
- Executive Master with 24ore Business School for non-profit operators:
  - 30 scholarships focused on digitalization and new technologies.
  - Objective to strengthen local social networks and structural alliances.
- Health and healthcare:
  - Support for construction of a new pediatric hemodialysis department at Bambino Gesù Children’s Hospital to improve care for young CKD patients (about 30,000 minors in Italy affected).
  - Five-month project completed in December 2024; improved facilities and family services; enhanced dialysis services for roughly 100 patients annually.
- Crowdfunding platforms:
  - Intesa Sanpaolo’s For Funding platform maintained a leading role in 2024, enabling free donations (bank covers 100% operating costs) across areas like poverty, healthcare, social inclusion, environment, and culture.
  - Rigorous NPO selection with branch and risk due diligence; donors can give via website/app; ongoing campaign communication.
  - “Formula” program supports high-impact local initiatives: every four months 13 NPOs are selected with CESVI’s technical support; projects receive co-funding and capacity-building.
  - 2024 results: around 8.7 million euro raised; approximately 6.1 million euro allocated to Formula; structured reporting and impact tracking required.
- Charity Allowance:
  - Governance: dedicated office (8 staff) and 23 Charity Representatives; support typically for one year, renewable up to three years; projects not exceeding 18 months except in exceptional cases.
  - 2024 disbursements: approximately 23 million euro to 814 NPO projects; about 934,000 direct beneficiaries (excluding medical research).
  - Priority lines (circa 40% of funds): combating educational poverty/digital divide; supporting NEETs and early school leavers (ELET); aiding women and children victims of violence and those facing discrimination.
  - Interventions include digital literacy, safe web use, STEAM labs, psychological support, personalized tutoring, soft-skill development, reclaimed learning spaces, and strong family/school engagement; focus on marginalized urban areas.
  - NEET/ELET actions: guidance, training, on-the-job learning (e.g., social agriculture, communication, emerging professions), targeted support for NEET mothers.
  - Anti-violence/discrimination: support for women victims, prisoners, migrants, people with disabilities/psychosocial fragilities, and LGBTQ+ persons; aims for safety, inclusion, and socio-economic autonomy; awareness and frontline worker training.
  - Additional areas: healthcare poverty, disease, disability, inclusive amateur sport, and socially beneficial cultural projects.
  - Medical research: 14 projects funded (1.6 million euro) selected with external expert review.
  - Social research: 4 studies (416 thousand euro) on gender violence (including foreign women), discrimination against women and gender/sexual minorities, health impacts of domestic violence, and youth gambling.
  - International scope: about 1.2 million euro disbursed within International Banks Division countries; new 2025–2026 Guidelines in development; 2025 resources to be approved with the 2024 financials.
  - Monitoring shows objectives largely met or exceeded, with strengthened local networks and sustained community impact; example partnerships include Piazza dei Mestieri with MIUR to counter school dropout.
- Demonstrated impacts:
  - Employment creation, social inclusion, policy influence, and territorial regeneration.
  - Example: GOEL Cooperativa Sociale in Calabria built ethical fashion and organic produce ventures challenging ’ndrangheta control, employing about 40 previously unemployed or vulnerable people.

nodes.title: Charity Allowance
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.6 Charity Allowance
nodes.start_phrase: The Chair's Technical Secretariat assists the Chair in the planning, implementation and monitoring of the Charity Allowance's initiatives through a dedicated office (Charity Allowance Office) made up of 8 resources.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and governance: The Charity Allowance, coordinated by the Chair’s Technical Secretariat (8 staff) and 23 Charity Representatives in the Banca dei Territori Division, plans, implements and monitors donations. Grants typically support one-year interventions (renewable up to three years, non-consecutively), with project durations capped at 18 months except in exceptional cases.
- 2024 scale and beneficiaries: About €23 million disbursed to 814 non-profit projects, reaching roughly 934,000 direct beneficiaries (excluding medical research). Around 40% of funds targeted three priority areas tied to recent health, economic and social crises.
- Priority areas and approaches:
  - Combating educational poverty and the digital divide: initiatives across all school levels, focus on migrant students and special needs, digital literacy and safe internet use, STEAM workshops, psychological support, personalized learning, soft skills development, community and family involvement, recovery of educational spaces, and public-private partnerships, especially in marginalized urban/suburban areas.
  - Support for NEETs and ELETs: personalized outreach, guidance, training and on-the-job learning (e.g., social agriculture, communication, emerging professions), with specific supports for NEET mothers to facilitate work-life balance.
  - Combating violence and discrimination: aid for women and children victims of violence, prisoners, migrants, individuals with disabilities/psychosocial fragilities, and LGBTQ+ people, aiming at safety, self-esteem, social inclusion and financial autonomy; awareness campaigns in schools and training for frontline workers.
- Other social focus areas: healthcare poverty, disease prevention, disability, inclusive amateur sports, and cultural projects with social outcomes.
- Research funding: Medical research—14 projects, €1.6 million, selected with external expert evaluations (objectives, methodology, impact, team, budget). Social research—€416,000 to four studies on gender-based violence against foreign women, discrimination/violence against women and gender/sexual minorities, cardiovascular/brain impacts of domestic violence and chronic stress, and youth gambling.
- International dimension: Collaboration with the International Banks Division, with ~€1.2 million disbursed in its geographies (about half of international donations). New 2025–2026 guidelines in development; 2025 resources to follow Board and Shareholders’ approvals alongside the 2024 Consolidated Financial Statements.
- Monitoring and results: Project checks show targets generally met or exceeded, strong community engagement, expanded local networks, and beneficiary numbers often above plans. Partnerships among social private sector, institutions, schools and services were consolidated, supporting long-term sustainability (e.g., Piazza dei Mestieri’s MoU with MIUR to curb dropouts).
- Illustrative impacts:
  - GOEL Cooperativa Sociale (Calabria): incubated ethical fashion and organic produce ventures countering ’ndrangheta control; ~40 jobs for vulnerable youth/adults.
  - Cooperativa Il Mandorlo (Lecce): trained 14 unemployed women in crafts; outcomes include self-entrepreneurship, employment, and university enrollment (supported 2020–2023).
  - FOQUS Centro Argo (Naples): non-medical center for people with cognitive disabilities; ~60 beneficiaries improved skills, internships started; school MoU for in-class therapeutic paths; renewed for third year.
  - Fondazione Pangea (Rome): emergency home for women victims of violence in Mafia-seized apartment; concrete exits from violence and employment; help desk for migrant women supported 120+; strong local networks; renewed for a second year.
- Implementation notes: Deadlines largely respected; typical first-year start-up delays and extended timelines for medical research to allow publication. International cooperation faced socio-political challenges mitigated by strong local presence and networks. Resources properly used; minor budget changes agreed with the Charity Allowance.
- Financial education and inclusion—Museo del Risparmio (Savings Museum):
  - Mission and reach: Edutainment-based financial literacy hub (Turin, founded 2012 within Intesa Sanpaolo), improving personal finance skills to reduce social exclusion; reached 100,548 users in 2024.
  - School programmes (aligned with new curricular mandates):
    - EduFin&Fun for primary/secondary: money basics, budgeting, safe internet, first online purchases.
    - PCTO (Path for Transversal Skills and Savings Orientation): six modular units totaling 60 hours, with special tracks for Fashion/Design and Sports high schools; digital content (e.g., educational games) for teachers. In 2024, 286 classes and 5,640 students participated.
  - Vulnerable groups (since 2017): tailored pilots for women, migrants, prisoners, disadvantaged students, people with mild cognitive disabilities. Key initiatives include:
    - Welcom-ed (migrants/CPIA and youth): basic financial terminology, budgeting, planning, and common financial instruments.
    - “Prometti di prenderti cura di te” (women victims of violence): financial skills for autonomy.
    - LEI and Logos (female inmates and ex-inmates): employability and recidivism prevention.
    - Additional activities for people with disabilities and those with drug/gambling addictions. In 2024, vulnerable-targeted training reached ~730 individuals.
  - Ongoing school engagement via storytelling, play, and edutainment-based projects.

nodes.title: Education and spread of financial culture
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.7 Education and spread of financial culture
nodes.start_phrase: Museo del Risparmio (Savings Museum) is an innovative space where it is possible to become familiar with the concepts of saving and investing with a clear and simple language, in order to improve the level of financial literacy of the people to w hom it is addressed.
nodes.summary:
- Social impact projects supported by Intesa Sanpaolo’s Charity Allowance:
  - Cooperativa Il Mandorlo (Lecce): training 14 unemployed women in tailoring, ceramics, carpentry; outcomes include self-entrepreneurship, employment, and university enrollment; supported over three years from 2020.
  - FOQUS – Centro Argo (Naples): non-medical center for people with cognitive disabilities; ~60 beneficiaries improved social/personal skills; internships activated; MoU with middle schools for in-class therapeutic paths; second year ended April 2024, renewed for third and final year.
  - Fondazione Pangea (Rome): emergency home for 15 women victims of violence and their children in an apartment seized from the Mafia; several women exited risk and gained employment; migrant women help desk supported 120+ beneficiaries; first year ended June 2024, renewed for a second year.
  - Project management: deadlines mostly met; initial-year launch delays and extensions typical for medical research; international cooperation faced socio-political challenges but was managed via local networks; resources used correctly with minor, agreed budget adjustments.

- Financial education and inclusion via Museo del Risparmio (Savings Museum):
  - Mission and reach: edutainment model to raise financial literacy; 100,548 users reached in 2024.
  - School programs aligned with new curricula:
    - EduFin&Fun (primary/secondary): money basics, budgeting, safe internet and first online purchases.
    - PCTO (secondary): six-module, 60-hour pathway with special tracks (Fashion/Design, Sports); 286 classes and 5,640 students in 2024; digital content (e.g., educational video games) for teachers.
  - Vulnerable groups (since 2017): migrants/foreign students (Welcom-ed), women victims of violence (Prometti di prenderti cura di te), female inmates/ex-inmates (LEI and Logos); ~730 beneficiaries in 2024; additional work with people with disabilities and addictions.
  - School-focused outreach: ECO-quiz at International Economics Festival (1,650 students); Safer Internet/Cybersecurity Month workshops (12,000+ students); career-awareness events (8,000+ students). Total 8,550 in-person and 80,184 remote participants; 1,070+ training hours.
  - International and adult outreach: FLITIN network workshops (6,250 students); 56 digital/blended adult events (3,735 participants; 2,900 on-demand views).
  - Youth collaboration: with Department for Youth Policies/Universal Civil Service for Carta Giovani holders; “Riscalda i muscoli” online course (20 dates; 4,591 participants).
  - Accessibility: content and tours for hearing/visual disabilities (with ENS and UICI).
  - Evidence-based design: annual surveys and third-party evaluations; latest (Nov 2024) on optimism, happiness, planning and financial peace of mind.
  - New formats/content in 2024: “Ammirare” VR exhibit linking art and economics; “La Scalata” escape room on financial planning; “Love station” video series; book “Un pizzico di economia.”

- Commitment to culture – Progetto Cultura (aligned with 2022–2025 Business Plan):
  - Gallerie d’Italia (Milan, Naples, Turin, Vicenza): bank buildings repurposed as museums; in 2024 delivered 12 major exhibitions; ~4,300 free educational visits/workshops for ~100,000 students; 690 inclusion courses (disabilities, refugees, mental health, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s) with 8,300 participants; 60+ public #Inside talks; app extended to all four venues.
  - Art assets management: 35,000 works under protection, conservation, research and enhancement; in 2024, 297 works loaned to 72 exhibitions; 10 long-term loans (126 works) to local entities; 253 maintenance/restoration interventions; regional enhancement with local foundations.
  - Restituzioni program (20th edition): restoration of 122 works across all 20 Italian regions plus an Italy–Belgium collaboration; 63 participating institutions; in partnership with 51 protection bodies and 57 restoration labs; over 2,200 works restored since inception.
  - Historical Archive: one of Europe’s leading bank archives, covering 20+ linear km; includes the Publifoto Archive; ongoing preservation, digitization, inventory and cataloguing activities.

nodes.title: Commitment to culture
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8 Commitment to culture
nodes.start_phrase: Intesa Sanpaolo supports the communities and territories in which it operates through a series of initiatives aimed at protecting and enhancing the historical, artistic and cultural heritage of both the country and the Group, primarily for the purpose of its public enjoyment for the benefit of the communities.
nodes.summary:
- The section outlines Intesa Sanpaolo’s “Commitment to culture” within its Consolidated Sustainability Statement, emphasizing support for communities by protecting and promoting historical, artistic, and cultural heritage for public benefit.
- Central to this is “Progetto Cultura,” a multi-year program aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan, developed with public and private partners at national and international levels to foster innovative, sustainable, and inclusive societies and strengthen stakeholder trust.
- Gallerie d’Italia: Four museum hubs in Milan, Naples, Turin, and Vicenza, created by transforming bank buildings into public museums. In 2024 they:
  - Hosted 12 major exhibitions with national/international partners, including ESG-themed photography in Turin.
  - Delivered around 4,300 free educational visits/workshops to nearly 100,000 students.
  - Ran 690 inclusive courses for people with disabilities and vulnerable groups (including refugees and those affected by mental health and neurodegenerative conditions), engaging 8,300 participants.
  - Held 60+ free #Inside public talks and expanded the Gallerie d’Italia App to all sites for enhanced digital visit experiences.
- Art assets: Stewardship of a 35,000-work corporate collection with ongoing protection, conservation, research, and public sharing via:
  - Loans of 297 works to 72 exhibitions in Italy and abroad.
  - 10 long-term loans (126 works) to local institutions.
  - 253 maintenance/restoration interventions.
  - Place-based enhancement initiatives with local foundations in Pistoia, Arezzo, Jesi, and Mirandola.
- Restituzioni program: Since 1989, supports restoration and enhancement of national heritage in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture.
  - In 2024 (20th edition): restoration of 122 works across all 20 Italian regions (plus an Italy–Belgium collaboration), involving 63 institutions, 51 protection entities, 57 restoration labs, and numerous specialists.
  - Over 2,200 artworks restored to date, “restituted” to communities to reinforce collective identity.
- Historical Archive: Management of one of Europe’s foremost banking archives, containing over 20 linear kilometers of historical documentation; includes the Publifoto photographic archive undergoing preservation, digitization, inventory, and cataloging activities.

nodes.title: Commitment to culture - Introduction
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8 Commitment to culture
nodes.start_phrase: Intesa Sanpaolo supports the communities and territories in which it operates through a series of initiatives aimed at protecting and enhancing the historical, artistic and cultural heritage of both the country and the Group, primarily for the purpose of its public enjoyment for the benefit of the communities.
nodes.summary: Intesa Sanpaolo’s “Progetto Cultura” is a multi-year programme aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan that supports communities by protecting and enhancing historical, artistic, and cultural heritage for public enjoyment. The initiative operates with public and private, national and international partners and includes Gallerie d’Italia (one of Europe’s most important private museums), management of the Bank’s art collections and Historical Archives, and the “Restituzioni” programme in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture to safeguard artistic and architectural assets. It also funds partnerships, sponsorships, and grants to build a collaborative cultural network. The programme aims to foster innovative, sustainable, and inclusive societies, strengthen local cultural identity, increase stakeholder trust, and contribute to business plan objectives.

nodes.title: Gallerie d’Italia
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8.1 Gallerie d’Italia
nodes.start_phrase: One of the main components of “Progetto Cultura” is “ Gallerie d'Italia”, the Intesa Sanpaolo museum hub resulting from the transformation of historic buildings owned by the Bank into museums open to cities to share the corporate collection, exhibit ions and initiatives of cultural and social value, linked to the territory and communities.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on Intesa Sanpaolo’s “Commitment to culture” within its Consolidated Sustainability Statement, highlighting culture as a lever for innovative, sustainable, and inclusive societies and alignment with the 2022–2025 Business Plan.
- Introduction of “Progetto Cultura,” a comprehensive program that promotes art and culture through partnerships with public and private institutions, manages the Bank’s art collections and Historical Archives, supports restorations, and fosters stakeholder trust.
- Gallerie d’Italia museum network (Milan, Naples, Turin, Vicenza): 12 major exhibitions in 2024, including ESG-themed photography in Turin; ~4,300 free educational visits/workshops engaging ~100,000 students; 690 inclusive courses for people with disabilities and vulnerable groups with 8,300 participants; over 60 free #Inside public talks; rollout of the Gallerie d’Italia App across all four sites.
- Stewardship of art assets: a 35,000-work corporate collection with ongoing conservation, research, and public sharing; 297 works loaned to 72 Italian and international exhibitions; 10 long-term loans (126 works) to local institutions; 253 maintenance/restoration actions; regional enhancement projects with local foundations (e.g., Pistoia, Arezzo, Jesi, Mirandola).
- “Restituzioni” program (since 1989): organization of the 20th edition restoring 122 works across all 20 Italian regions (plus an Italy–Belgium collaboration), involving 63 entities, 51 Ministry of Culture protection bodies, 57 restoration labs, and hundreds of specialists; more than 2,200 assets “returned” to communities over 35 years.
- Historical Archive management: one of Europe’s foremost banking archives with over 20 linear km of records, including the Publifoto Archive, undergoing preservation, digitization, inventorying, and cataloguing to document the Bank’s and Italy’s history.

nodes.title: Art assets
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8.2 Art assets
nodes.start_phrase: Intesa Sanpaolo demonstrates a strong commitment to the care and enhancement of the Group's art collections, made up of 35 thousand works, which represent one of the most important corporate collections in Europe in terms of size and quality.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Intesa Sanpaolo’s “Commitment to culture” within its Consolidated Sustainability Statement, centered on Progetto Cultura, which protects and enhances cultural heritage, expands public access, fosters inclusive and sustainable societies, strengthens stakeholder trust, and aligns with the 2022–2025 Business Plan.
- Progetto Cultura pillars:
  - Gallerie d’Italia: Four museum hubs in Milan, Naples, Turin, and Vicenza created from historic bank buildings; 2024 program featured 12 major exhibitions with national/international partners (including ESG-focused photography in Turin), ~4,300 free educational visits/workshops for nearly 100,000 students, inclusion initiatives with 690 courses for people with disabilities and vulnerable groups (8,300 participants), 60+ free #Inside public talks, and rollout of the Gallerie d’Italia app to all sites.
  - Art assets: Stewardship of a 35,000-work corporate collection through protection, conservation, research, and sharing; in 2024, 297 works loaned to 72 Italian and international exhibitions, 10 loans totaling 126 works to local institutions, 253 maintenance/restoration actions, and targeted local partnerships with foundations (e.g., Pistoia, Arezzo, Jesi, Mirandola).
  - Restituzioni: Long-running program (since 1989) with the Ministry of Culture to restore and return artworks to communities; 2024’s 20th edition covers 122 works from all 20 Italian regions plus an Italy–Belgium collaboration, engaging 63 institutions, 51 protection entities, 57 restoration labs, and hundreds of experts; over 2,200 assets restored to date.
  - Historical Archive: Management of one of Europe’s foremost banking archives (20+ linear km of records), including the Publifoto photographic collection, with ongoing protection, conservation, digitization, inventory, and cataloging work.
- Cross-cutting aims: Public sharing of assets, educational outreach, social inclusion (disability, refugees, mental health), digital accessibility, and broad collaboration through partnerships, sponsorships, and grants.

nodes.title: Restituzioni
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8.3 Restituzioni
nodes.start_phrase: Again within the scope of “Progetto Cultura”, Intesa Sanpaolo, in dialogue with the Ministry of Culture and the bodies responsible for artistic heritage protection, has supported and managed the “Restituzioni” programme since 1989, dedicated to the restoration and enhancement of the national heritage.
nodes.summary:
- Section focus: Intesa Sanpaolo’s Commitment to Culture within the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.
- Progetto Cultura: the Bank’s multi-year cultural program aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan to protect and enhance historical, artistic, and cultural heritage for public benefit, foster innovative, sustainable, and inclusive societies, build stakeholder trust, and develop partnerships, sponsorships, and grants with public and private entities nationally and internationally.
- Gallerie d’Italia: a museum hub created by converting Bank-owned historic buildings into public museums in Milan, Naples, Turin, and Vicenza; regarded as one of Europe’s most important private museum initiatives.
- 2024 Gallerie d’Italia impact: 12 major exhibitions with national/international partners; Turin photography shows commissioned on ESG themes.
- Education and outreach: ~4,300 free visits/workshops serving nearly 100,000 students of all ages, offering engaging experiences to build cultural awareness and a sense of shared history.
- Inclusion: 690 courses designed for people with disabilities or in vulnerable situations (including refugees and people from diverse cultures; focus on mental health, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s), engaging 8,300 participants.
- Public programming and access: 60+ free #Inside talks; Gallerie d’Italia app extended to all four sites, offering free audio/video content for an enhanced digital visit.
- Art assets stewardship: care and enhancement of a 35,000‑work corporate collection with ongoing protection, conservation, research, and valorization.
- 2024 loans and conservation: 297 works lent to 72 Italian and international exhibitions (e.g., Scuderie del Quirinale, National Gallery London); 10 loans totaling 126 works to local institutions; 253 maintenance/restoration interventions.
- Local collaborations: projects in culturally significant territories with banking foundations (Pistoia/Fondazione Caript, Arezzo/Fondazione Bruschi, Jesi/Fondazione CR Jesi, Mirandola/Fondazione CR Mirandola).
- Restituzioni program: since 1989, supports restoration and enhancement of national heritage; 20th edition (2024) covers 122 works from all 20 Italian regions plus an Italy–Belgium collaboration, involving 63 entities, 51 Ministry protection bodies, 57 restoration labs, and hundreds of experts; over 2,200 works restored and returned to communities over 35 years.
- Historical Archive: one of Europe’s foremost bank archives with 20+ linear km of records; includes the Publifoto Archive; ongoing protection, conservation, digitization, inventory, and cataloguing activities.

nodes.title: Historical archive
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8.4 Historical archive
nodes.start_phrase: “Progetto Cultura” also manages the Group's Historical Archive, one of the first and most important bank archives in Europe, a valuable heritage for reconstructing not only the history of the Bank, but also the history of the entire country.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Intesa Sanpaolo’s strategic commitment to culture as a lever for innovative, sustainable, and inclusive societies, aligned with the 2022–2025 Business Plan and aimed at strengthening stakeholder trust and community value.
- Progetto Cultura: The Group’s umbrella program for cultural initiatives, developed with public/private, national/international partners; manages museums, art collections, restorations, archives, partnerships, and education.
- Gallerie d’Italia (Milan, Naples, Turin, Vicenza): Bank-owned historic buildings transformed into public museums; in 2024 delivered 12 major exhibitions, 4,300 free educational activities involving ~100,000 students; strong inclusion programming (690 courses; 8,300 participants) addressing disability, refugees, multiculturalism, and mental health; 60+ free #Inside talks; app-based digital guide active in all four sites.
- Art assets: One of Europe’s largest corporate collections (35,000 works); 2024 loans of 297 works to 72 shows in Italy and abroad; 10 multi-work loans (126 works) to local entities; 253 conservation/restoration actions; territorial enhancement with local foundations (Pistoia, Arezzo, Jesi, Mirandola).
- Restituzioni: Long-running restoration program with the Ministry of Culture; 20th edition underway restoring 122 works from all 20 regions (+ one Italy–Belgium case); 63 participating institutions, 51 protection bodies, 57 labs; over 2,200 works “restituted” to communities since 1989.
- Historical Archive: Among Europe’s leading bank archives (20+ linear km); 2024 digitization of 470,000 pages (1M+ pages online total) and 11,000 new inventory records; Publifoto Archive: +5,000 photos digitized (~60,000 total; ~33,000 online) and ~24,000 catalog records; open data, education, inclusion projects (Art & People), and sustained digital outreach.
- Partnerships/sponsorships/donations: Extensive collaborations with foundations, major fairs/exhibitions (Miart, Artissima, Venice Biennale Holy See Pavilion, Salone del Libro), festivals (Cortona On The Move, Archivissima, Milano Musica), and museums (Egyptian Museum Turin, Poldi Pezzoli, Palazzo Strozzi); municipal collaborations; Art Bonus support (GAMeC, Amatrice church, Egyptian Museum courtyard, Sant’Aspreno in Naples, Mondovì Historical Fund).
- Higher education/cultural professions: Gallerie d’Italia Academy executive course (29 students; 60+ faculty; 8 scholarships; 162 hours; in-person/webinars; Alumni network); Euploos Project for Uffizi drawings (2024: 2,252 records, 3,250 images; overall 73,500 works online, 9,600 with scientific records); collaborations with IED and IAAD; >120 young art historians employed via Civita.
- Institutional community initiatives: Projects to engage youth with opera/music/art (e.g., Teatro alla Scala “UNDER 30”), plus support for film/science culture (Turin Film Festival, BergamoScienza).
- Social solidarity: Support for the “Costruiamo il Futuro” Award aiding small non-profits in Lombardy; broader areas of intervention include culture, environment/sustainability, production ecosystem dialogue, social inclusion, sport, and health.

nodes.title: Partnerships, sponsorships, donations
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8.5 Partnerships, sponsorships, donations
nodes.start_phrase: The Bank supports artistic -cultural, social and training initiatives through forms of collaboration with public and private entities, where its contribution often takes the form of sharing and co -designing contents, spaces and relationships.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on cultural heritage digitization and access: expansion of the Bank’s Historical Archive using advanced digital tools (e.g., Linked Open Data) and a public portal; in 2024, 470,000 additional pages digitized (now over 1 million online) and 11,000 new inventory record cards; continuation of research and enhancement projects (e.g., Egeli Project on 1939–1945 Jewish asset seizures with Fondazione 1563); educational outreach to university and school students.
- Publifoto Archive progress: over 5,000 new photos digitized (circa 60,000 total, ~33,000 online) and about 24,000 new catalog records.
- Inclusion and people engagement: initiatives around Bank-owned art and archives involving Group employees, emphasizing accessibility, inclusion, diversity, and multiculturalism (Art & People); continued original content on Gallerie d’Italia and Group digital channels to broaden access and engagement.
- Partnerships, sponsorships, and donations: collaborations with banking foundations (Compagnia di San Paolo, Cariplo, Cariparo, CR Firenze, CR Forlì); support for major fairs and festivals (Miart, Artissima, Holy See Pavilion at Venice Biennale, Salone del Libro, Cortona On The Move, Archivissima, Milano Musica); museum synergies (Egyptian Museum Turin, Poldi Pezzoli, Palazzo Strozzi); support for municipal Christmas exhibitions (Milan, Vicenza); co-organized shows (Cuneo with Fondazione CR Cuneo; Merate with Fondazione Costruiamo il Futuro); Art Bonus-backed public heritage projects (GaMec new venue, Amatrice church reconstruction, Egyptian Museum courtyard renovation, Church of Sant’Aspreno ai Crociferi restoration in Naples, enhancement of Mondovì Historical Fund).
- Youth and public engagement in culture: initiatives with leading cultural institutions to attract new generations to opera, music, art; collaborations with theatres (e.g., Teatro alla Scala’s “La Scala UNDER 30”) and support for science and film events (Turin Film Festival, BergamoScienza).
- Higher education and cultural professions: 4th edition of Gallerie d’Italia Academy Executive course on management of artistic-cultural heritage and corporate collections, in partnership with key foundations and the Ministry of Culture’s training body; 29 students, ~60 instructors, 8 scholarships, 162 hours (in-person Milan/Turin and online); ongoing alumni community for training/networking. Conclusion of the Euploos Project with the Uffizi (2024 outputs: 2,252 scientific records, 3,250 images; overall catalogue: 73,500 works, 9,600 with scientific records). Collaborations with design schools (IED, IAAD) and employment of 120+ young art historians via Civita Mostre e Musei at Gallerie d’Italia.
- Community-oriented institutional initiatives: partnership and sponsorship selection aligned with ethical, cultural, and social values; priority areas include culture, environment and sustainability, industry dialogue, social inclusion, sport, and health.
- Social solidarity: support for the “Costruiamo il Futuro” Award aiding small non-profit organizations in Lombardy (text continues).

nodes.title: Higher education and enhancement of cultural professions
nodes.heading: 4.3.2.4.8.6 Higher education and enhancement of cultural professions
nodes.start_phrase: Intesa Sanpaolo promotes training and skill development projects in the arts and culture, with a particular focus on young people, in recognition of the potential of cultural heritage, also as a driver of economic and employment growth.
nodes.summary:
- Archival digitization and public access: expanded digital access using technologies like LinkedOpenData and a dedicated portal; in 2024 digitized 470,000 additional pages (now over 1 million online) and created 11,000 new inventory record cards; continued research and enhancement projects (e.g., “Egeli Project” on 1939–1945 Jewish asset seizures with Fondazione 1563); education initiatives to engage university and school students. Publifoto Archive: over 5,000 new photos digitized (about 60,000 total; ~33,000 online) and ~24,000 new catalog records.

- Inclusion and employee engagement: initiatives around Bank-owned art and archives involving Group employees on accessibility, inclusion, diversity, and multiculturalism (Art & People); ongoing production of original digital content via Gallerie d’Italia and Group channels to broaden access and participation.

- Partnerships, sponsorships, and donations: co-designed cultural, social, and training projects with public and private partners. 2024 highlights include collaborations with major banking foundations (Compagnia di San Paolo, Cariplo, Cariparo, CR Firenze, CR Forlì), leading fairs/exhibitions (Miart, Artissima, Holy See Pavilion at the Venice Biennale, Salone Internazionale del Libro), and festivals (Cortona On The Move, Archivissima, Milano Musica). Synergies with key museums (Egyptian Museum Turin, Poldi Pezzoli Milan, Palazzo Strozzi Florence); support for municipal Christmas exhibitions (Milan, Vicenza); co-organized shows (Cuneo with Fondazione CRC; Merate with Fondazione Costruiamo il Futuro). Art Bonus projects for public heritage (GaMec new venue, Amatrice church reconstruction, Egyptian Museum courtyard renovation, Church of Sant’Aspreno ai Crociferi restoration in Naples, enhancement of Mondovì Historical Fund).

- Cultural outreach to new generations: institutional initiatives with leading cultural bodies to bring youth closer to opera, music, and art (e.g., Teatro alla Scala’s “La Scala UNDER 30”), plus support for cultural, science, and film events (Turin Film Festival, BergamoScienza).

- Higher education and cultural professions: training programs prioritizing young talent. Gallerie d’Italia Academy Executive Course (4th edition, 2024) on management of cultural heritage and corporate collections with major foundations and the Ministry of Culture—29 students, ~60 instructors, 8 scholarships, 162 hours (in-person and webinars), hosted at Bank venues in Milan and Turin; ongoing alumni community for continuous learning and networking. Completion of the “Euploos Project” (Uffizi drawings digital catalogue): in 2024 produced 2,252 scientific records and 3,250 images; overall 73,500 works online, >9,600 with scientific records. Collaborations with design schools (IED, IAAD). Over 120 young art historians engaged at Gallerie d’Italia via Civita Mostre e Musei.

- Community and sustainability commitment: selection of initiatives aligned with the Bank’s ethical, cultural, and social values. 2024 focus areas: culture; environment and sustainability; engagement with the productive sector; social inclusion; sport and health promotion.

- Social solidarity: support for the “Costruiamo il Futuro” Award aiding small non-profit organizations in Lombardy.
